goal:
Make in-assignment transient backend errors non-fatal to the runner (S4).

Source research: task 2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4 ("noticing a high level of interruptions"). Read docs/tasks/2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4/RESPONSE.md, docs/tasks/2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4/WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md, docs/tasks/2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4/TDD-TEST-EXAMPLES.md and the cited GUIDE before coding. Survey answers (if any) live in docs/tasks/2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4/RESPONSE_SURVEY.md. Section: RESPONSE.md S4, docs/tasks/2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4/GUIDE-04-backend-unreachable-502.md, WIDE_NET Cause 4. Survey: q5 (survive network/502/503/504, keep the rest fatal).

Evidence: "501 fetch failed + 16 Backend 502 since 11-19 on server2-alpha; a proven 502 window 11-20 20:40:20-20:40:57 during backend build 637. Today any in-try backend-call failure inside executeAssignment sends an interrupt and rethrows -> process exit -> systemd restart. Heartbeat failures are tolerated (lease TTL) but in-assignment call failures are fatal, so every LAN blip or backend restart window can kill a run."

MUST-READ BEFORE CODING: docs/tasks/db49d6c6-*/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md (runner recovery containment) - build on it or explicitly scope against it; do NOT land a second competing catch-restructure.

Change (runner, runner/daemon.js + runner/client.js): (1) executeAssignment catch (runner/daemon.js:2299-2452): transient backend errors (fetch failed network errors, 502/503/504) during an assignment send interrupt WITH reason and RETURN (keep polling) instead of rethrowing - same report-and-return precedent as WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED and deterministic-gitFailure branches. (2) bounded retries with backoff for idempotent calls (heartbeat, dispatch poll) so idle loop stops crash-cycling (restart counters 366->367 in 11-19 sample) - or at minimum sleep-and-continue instead of exit. (3) keep FATAL: STALE_EPOCH, auth failures, genuinely unknown errors - enumerate the non-fatal set explicitly, never invert the catch-all, so new failure modes stay loud.

Tests: runner/client.backendOutage.test.js (GUIDE-04 section 2: 502 shape, dropped-socket shape, recovery) + section 3 fatality-boundary test flipped red (expect(rethrown).toBe(false) transient, still-true stale-epoch). Register in scripts/run-tests.mjs. Confirm: E4 timestamp-join on db24c124, 1f8959ca, f56e9878, ef21e99b, bae668cb (PROD-READ-ONLY, needs permission); after rollout, crash-restart rate in runner journal drops while assignment success holds.

reports.content:
# Code-standards review — S4 branch vs `main` (this task's branch)

Task: `78eac844-250a-44d1-810e-6f047eb5a59e` — "Make in-assignment transient backend errors non-fatal to the runner (S4)". Branch `kb/78eac844-250a-44d1-810e-6f047eb5a59e` reviewed against `main` (`origin/main` / `main`; there is no `master` ref in this checkout — `main` is the comparison base). Standards file: `docs/KB Code Standards.md`, read together with its referenced detailed copy `docs/agent-docs/KB-Code-Standards.md` (§Documentation/Jsdoc). This stage is docs-only; no source was modified — this review was produced by read-only inspection and test runs.

## Scope reviewed (`git diff main...HEAD --stat`)

- `runner/client.js` (+53) — new `TRANSIENT_BACKEND_STATUSES`, `TRANSIENT_NETWORK_CODES`, exported `isTransientBackendError(err)`.
- `runner/daemon.js` (+159) — new `retryTransient`, `describeBackendOutageCause`; transient branches in `joinAndHeartbeat`, `executeAssignment`, `executeIntegrationAssignment`, `runSingleAssignment`, `runDispatchLoop`.
- `runner/client.backendOutage.test.js` (new, 202 lines), `runner/daemon.test.js` (+580), `scripts/run-tests.mjs` (registration), `publish.sh` (runner gate registration), `runner/README.md` (failure-handling note), `runner/version.json` (`0.2.0` -> `0.2.1`).
- Task docs under `docs/tasks/78eac844-250a-44d1-810e-6f047eb5a59e/` (implementation plan, survey, upgrade-safety review, two auto-generated reports).

The diff does **not** restructure the db49d6c6 dispatch-loop catch, per the MUST-READ constraint — verified by grep of the `runner/daemon.js` diff (only additive branches; the `else { throw err }` tail and `STALE_EPOCH` propagation remain).

## Verdict: PASS — no blocking standards violation found

Each standard below was checked against the actual diff and test runs. Minor observations are listed as notes, not failures.

### Values — user understandable over technical language

- **Long descriptive names — pass.** New identifiers are descriptive: `TRANSIENT_BACKEND_STATUSES`, `TRANSIENT_NETWORK_CODES`, `describeBackendOutageCause`, `retryTransient`, `callBackend`, `waitsMs`. The user-facing interrupt reason is plain English: `` `Backend unreachable mid-assignment: ${...}` `` (`runner/daemon.js:2513`, `:2787`) and the dispatch log `Dispatch: backend unreachable (...)` — no invented abstractions.
- **Technical language — pass.** No new "factory"/"barrel"/pattern vocabulary. A case-insensitive grep for `factory|Singleton|Strategy|Observer|design pattern` over `runner/client.js` + `runner/daemon.js` finds only the pre-existing comment "module singleton" (`runner/daemon.js:1055`), untouched by this branch. The word "transient" is the domain term from the task brief, used consistently with the test file header (`GUIDE-04 section 2/3` references) and `runner/README.md`.
- **Common language profile — pass.** `task`, `assignment`, `runner`, `backend`, `interrupt` are used in their established senses; nothing is renamed.
- **File structure reflects call stack — pass.** The classifier lives in `runner/client.js` (the file that defines the `{ statusCode, code }` vs raw-fetch-rejection error shapes) and `runner/daemon.js` imports it (`runner/daemon.js:47`). This is the correct call-hierarchy direction (daemon -> client), not an inversion.
- **JSDoc plain English + `@example` + MARK — pass, gate-verified.** Every new export/helper carries `MARK:` + `@description` + `@example` + `@param`/`@returns`:
  - `MARK: isTransientBackendError` (`runner/client.js:24-38`) with `@example isTransientBackendError(Object.assign(new Error('x'), { statusCode: 502 })) => true`,
  - `MARK: retryTransient` (`runner/daemon.js:1106-1121`),
  - `MARK: describeBackendOutageCause` (`runner/daemon.js:1135-1149`),
  - new suite header `MARK: backend-outage tests` (`runner/client.backendOutage.test.js:5-11`).
  - Live gate: `node scripts/check-jsdoc-example.mjs` -> `jsdoc-@example: PASS (679 missing, baseline (680 grandfathered))`. The new export is not added to the grandfather baseline, as the standard requires.
- **Why, not just what — pass.** JSDoc and inline comments explain the reason: e.g. client.js "Deliberately NOT matched: bare TypeError: fetch failed ... ambiguous failures stay loud rather than spinning the loop forever"; daemon.js "Bounded by construction, never infinite ... so a caller bug can never mask the backend's answer"; "The `transient` flag is additive and internal". The README note explains the ride-through in operator terms.
- **Labelled data-inport pattern `({varA,varB}) => {}` — pass (one acceptable note).** The two daemon helpers follow it exactly: `retryTransient({ callBackend, waitsMs = [] } = {})` (`runner/daemon.js:1121`), `describeBackendOutageCause({ error } = {})` (`runner/daemon.js:1149`). Note: `isTransientBackendError(err)` (`runner/client.js:38`) takes a single positional parameter. This matches existing repo precedent for one-argument predicates (`isModelsPinned(config)`, `isRunnableFile(...)`) and satisfies "Give the minimum data to each function" — a single-error predicate has no second field to label. Not a violation.

### Functional over object-oriented

- **No classes, no pattern framing — pass.** `grep -n "^class "` over both runtime files returns nothing. Functions are plain `function`/`async function` declarations, black-box with explicit inputs.
- **Black-box / immutable — pass.** `isTransientBackendError` is a pure predicate ("no logging, no dependencies" in its own description) that only reads `statusCode`/`code`/`cause.code`. `describeBackendOutageCause` only reads and redacts. Return values in the transient branches are fresh literals (`{ interrupted: true, executionId, epoch, reason, transient: true }` at `runner/daemon.js:2521` and `:2796`) — no mutation of shared state; the `transient` flag is additive/internal as the plan specified.
- **Verb-named functions — pass with note.** `retryTransient` and `describeBackendOutageCause` begin with verbs. `isTransientBackendError` is an `is-` predicate; the standard's "always named with a verb" is strictly a deviation here, but it follows the file's established predicate convention (`isModelsPinned`, `isRunnableFile`) — changing a predicate to a verb would break the convention the standard also asks for ("common language profile"). Not a failing violation.

### Co-location over abstraction

- **Tests next to the file — pass.** New `runner/client.backendOutage.test.js` sits beside `runner/client.js`; daemon boundary tests are appended in `runner/daemon.test.js` beside the existing `runDispatchLoop`/`runSingleAssignment` blocks, reusing `stubClient`/`fakeHarness`/`loopConfig`.
- **Helpers at the lowest common folder — pass.** `retryTransient`/`describeBackendOutageCause` are defined in `runner/daemon.js` (their sole user) and `isTransientBackendError` in `runner/client.js` (owner of the error shapes). No `shared/` leakage for a runner-only concern.
- **Abstraction only when repeated / non-trivial — pass.** Both helpers are used three times each (register, heartbeat, dispatch poll for `retryTransient`; executeAssignment, executeIntegrationAssignment, dispatch backoff for `describeBackendOutageCause`) and each contains non-trivial logic (a bounded retry loop with `isTransientBackendError` gate; a cause-chain walk), so they clear the standard's "don't abstract a single line unless it has complex logic" bar. Both mirror an existing sibling shape (`WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` report-and-return, 429/`RUNNER_PAUSED` backoff) rather than inventing a layer.
- **Searchability — pass.** `isTransientBackendError` is the single grep-able home for the non-fatal set; all four catch sites call it. No status/close-code checks are duplicated inline.

### Tested over trusted

- **Tests planned and evidenced — pass, verified by execution in this review:**
  - `node --test runner/client.backendOutage.test.js` -> 9 pass / 0 fail (classifier boundary: gateway positives, socket-code positives incl. nested/cyclic causes, STALE_EPOCH/auth/429/500/501 negatives, bare-`fetch failed` stays loud; wire shapes: 502 json + proxy-HTML, 503/504, dropped socket, recovery).
  - `node --test runner/daemon.test.js` -> 180 pass / 0 fail, including the S4 boundary tests (transient returns with interrupt-with-reason and loop keeps polling; STALE_EPOCH/auth/unknown still rethrow; join ride-through and exhaustion; dispatch backoff without consuming idle budget; integration parity).
  - `node --test runner/client.test.js` -> 16 pass / 0 fail (no disturbance to existing client shapes).
  - Registration pins now green: `node --test tests/publish.test.mjs tests/run-tests.test.mjs` -> 68 pass / 0 fail. (The earlier `automated-tests-failure-20261123-092217.md` Harness-Self-Tests failure was the `publish.sh` runner gate missing the new suite; the current HEAD registers it in both `scripts/run-tests.mjs` and `publish.sh` and the pin passes — resolved, not open.)
- **Lowest level first, black-box, user-shaped — pass.** The outage suite exercises the real `createRunnerClient.call` path with a stubbed `fetchImpl` (GUIDE-04 §2 shapes); daemon tests drive real `runDispatchLoop`/`runSingleAssignment` with temp git repos and a fake harness (lowest level that proves the loop behavior; no live AI agent, no ports). Assertions are primarily behavioral (returned vs rethrown, interrupt carried the reason, assignments continue); the two log-capture assertions confirm the survey q4 "one-line note naming the cause" — consistent with "failures should be clear, transparent and observable" and with the existing suite's logger-capture style.
- **Fatality boundary is explicit — pass.** The classifier enumerates 502/503/504 + named network codes and falls through to false for everything else (STALE_EPOCH 409, 401/403, 429, 500, 501, unknown, non-thrown values). Tests pin both sides, including the flipped-red boundary (`rethrown === false` transient / `true` stale-epoch) by behavior, so new failure modes stay loud by construction.

### Fast iteration / blast radius

- The change is additive and narrow: no new dependencies or flags, no wire/schema change (`reason` field already existed), version bump `0.2.0` -> `0.2.1` with unchanged `requires.backendApi`, matching the upgrade-safety review (`UPGRADE-SAFETY-REVIEW.md` verdict PASS). The only error-text change an existing install could observe is the single-shot failure message (`Backend unreachable mid-assignment: ...` instead of the raw 502) — still a non-zero exit, noted there as not an install break.

## Notes (non-blocking, no action required unless a future edit touches the file)

1. `isTransientBackendError(err)` is positional while sibling helpers use the labelled object pattern — acceptable for a single-argument predicate (see above); a future multi-field extension should adopt `{ error }`.
2. `catch (err)` / `err` short names follow the surrounding file's convention (94 occurrences in `runner/daemon.js`); the standard's "long names where needed" is satisfied by the descriptive module-level identifiers.
3. `describeBackendOutageCause` mirrors the classifier's cause-chain walk (depth 4 in both). The duplication is 6 lines and flagged by its own comment; the standard's "don't fear repetition" permits it, and a shared walk helper would risk drifting on the deliberately-different semantics (first-found code vs recognized code).

## Evidence trail

- Diff base: `main` (no `master` ref exists in this checkout); `git diff main...HEAD --stat` = 15 files, 2644 insertions, 11 deletions — only the runner, its gates, README, version, and task docs.
- Gates run in this review: `node scripts/check-jsdoc-example.mjs` PASS; `run-tests`/`publish` pin tests 68 pass; `client.backendOutage` 9 pass; `client` 16 pass; `daemon` 180 pass.

KAINBAIN_VERDICT: PASS

# Implementation Plan — In-assignment transient backend errors non-fatal to the runner (S4)

Task: `78eac844-250a-44d1-810e-6f047eb5a59e`
Source problem: any in-try backend-call failure inside `executeAssignment` sends an interrupt and rethrows → process exit → systemd restart, so every LAN blip or backend restart window can kill a run (501 fetch failed + 16 Backend 502s since 11-19 on server2-alpha; proven 502 window 11-20 20:40:20–20:40:57 during backend build 637).
Survey input: [SURVEY.md](./SURVEY.md) (Round 1, q1–q4; `answers: {}` — unanswered, so the recommended options below are carried as assumptions pending confirmation).

## Goal

1. Transient backend errors (fetch-failed network errors, HTTP 502/503/504) raised during an assignment make `executeAssignment` send an interrupt WITH a reason and RETURN (keep polling) instead of rethrowing — the same report-and-return precedent as the `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` and deterministic-gitFailure branches.
2. The idle loop stops crash-cycling on backend outages: bounded retries with backoff for idempotent calls (dispatch poll; heartbeat already warn-continues), or at minimum sleep-and-continue instead of exit.
3. The non-fatal set is enumerated explicitly; `STALE_EPOCH`, auth failures, and genuinely unknown errors stay fatal. No inverted catch-all, so new failure modes stay loud.
4. Regression tests in `runner/client.backendOutage.test.js` (+ daemon fatality-boundary tests) prove the transient/fatal boundary, registered in `scripts/run-tests.mjs`.

## Success Criteria

- A 502/503/504 or dropped-socket failure from any backend call inside `executeAssignment` produces a best-effort `interrupt` carrying a reason, a one-line log naming the cause, and a return (no throw) — the dispatch loop keeps polling and the process stays alive.
- A dispatch-poll (`dispatchClaim`) transient failure backs off and re-polls without consuming idle budget and without exiting; restart counters stop incrementing across a backend restart window.
- `STALE_EPOCH` still propagates (epoch fencing intact), auth/credential failures still exit loud, and unknown errors still throw — proven by boundary tests asserting `rethrown === false` for transient and `rethrown === true` for stale-epoch.
- `node --test runner/client.backendOutage.test.js runner/daemon.test.js runner/client.test.js` passes, the repo unit gate (`npm test` via `scripts/run-tests.mjs`) passes, and the new suite file is registered (the `tests/run-tests.test.mjs` pin fails the gate if it is not).
- Post-rollout (needs PROD-READ-ONLY permission): crash-restart rate in the runner journal drops across backend restart windows while assignment success holds; E4 timestamp-join confirmed on `db24c124`, `1f8959ca`, `f56e9878`, `ef21e99b`, `bae668cb`.

## Survey decisions (factored in)

Local `SURVEY.md` Round 1 is unanswered (`"answers": {}`). This plan adopts the recommended option for each as a working assumption (flagged for confirmation in Open Questions). The stage brief also cites the source-task survey q5 ("survive network/502/503/504, keep the rest fatal") — that maps to local q2 and is adopted the same way.

| # | Question | Adopted (recommended) answer | Plan effect |
|---|----------|------------------------------|-------------|
| q1 | Mid-task connection drop: what should the worker do? | Stay alive, report what happened, keep checking for work | Interrupt-with-reason + return; never rethrow for the transient set. |
| q2 (= source q5) | Which problems to survive vs still stop for? | Only survive short connection problems (network errors, 502/503/504); still stop for login problems, outdated orders, anything unknown | Explicit non-fatal enumeration (`isTransientBackendError`); `STALE_EPOCH`/auth/unknown stay fatal. |
| q3 | Idle poll/heartbeat outage: what to do? | Retry a few times with growing waits, then keep waiting without restarting | Bounded retries with backoff on idempotent idle calls; minimum acceptable fallback is sleep-and-continue. |
| q4 (optional) | Log visibility for ride-through? | A clear one-line note naming the cause, then keep going | One `warn`/`error` line with cause + task/project IDs per ride-through; no per-retry spam (retry attempts at debug/quiet). |

## Approach

Follow "make the change easy, then make the change", and build on the db49d6c6 containment — do NOT land a second competing catch-restructure:

1. **Easy first:** extract one shared `isTransientBackendError(err)` classifier (single home for the explicit non-fatal set) plus shared test fixtures (502-shape stub, dropped-socket stub), with zero behavior change. Land this refactor green before touching behavior.
2. **Then the change:** add one narrow branch in the `executeAssignment` catch using the classifier (interrupt-with-reason + return), mirroring the `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` block shape; same one-branch treatment for the `executeIntegrationAssignment` catch (parity, decided in Key Decision 4).
3. **Then the idle loop:** transient-aware handling in the `dispatchClaim` catch (backoff + re-poll, no idle-budget consumption); verify the heartbeat timer path already tolerates outages (it warns-and-continues today) and add bounded join-time retries only if the Step 0 probe shows join is a live crash path.
4. **Then proof:** `runner/client.backendOutage.test.js` + daemon boundary tests, registration in `scripts/run-tests.mjs`, red→green runs, full gates, rollout/confirm plan.

No new dependencies, no new config flags (backoff constants are module-local), no schema/wire changes (the interrupt `reason` field already exists).

## Evidence (what the research established)

Verified in-repo this session (line numbers are the current checkout — re-verify at implementation time):

- **In-assignment catch:** `executeAssignment` catch (`runner/daemon.js` ~2296–2453) special-cases `STALE_EPOCH` (rethrow, line 2298), `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` (interrupt-with-reason + return, lines 2299–2315), deterministic gitFailure (report + return, lines 2316–2376), `failedOutcome` (failed completion, lines 2377–2428), then the generic path: flush, best-effort interrupt with reason, **`throw err`** (lines 2441–2452). The S4 branch slots in just before the generic path, copying the `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` block shape.
- **db49d6c6 containment already landed (build on it):** `runDispatchLoop` wraps `executeAssignment` in try/catch (~3097–3153): `STALE_EPOCH` rethrows, anything else is logged and contained. So in dispatch mode a rethrow no longer exits — but the stage brief's crash path is still live in three places: (a) `dispatchClaim` unknown errors `throw err` at line 3018 → loop exits → systemd restart (this is the 366→367 crash-cycling); (b) `runSingleAssignment` has no loop, so any rethrow exits non-zero; (c) `joinAndHeartbeat` failures before the loop starts exit the process. S4 must target exactly these, not rework the db49 catch.
- **Client error shapes** (`runner/client.js` `call`, lines 17–40): non-2xx throws `Error` with `statusCode = res.status` and `code = data?.code ?? null` — so a 502 arrives as `{ statusCode: 502, code }`. A dropped socket / refused connection rejects `fetchImpl` itself (raw `TypeError: fetch failed`, `ECONNREFUSED`/`ECONNRESET` causes) with no `statusCode`. The classifier must cover both shapes.
- **Heartbeat already tolerates outages:** the periodic timer (`deliverSteers(...).catch(warn)`, lines 1241–1245) and claim renewal (`claimHeartbeat(...).then(warn)`, lines 796–808) both warn-and-continue; heartbeat failures ride the lease TTL. The idle-loop crash-cycling is the dispatch-poll path, not the heartbeat path.
- **Integration parity site:** `executeIntegrationAssignment` catch (~2655–2697) ends in the same interrupt + `throw err` (lines 2687–2696).
- **Fatality contract pinned by an existing test:** `runner/daemon.test.js` "never idles out with dispatchIdleLimit 0" throws a generic `persistent-loop-probe` error from `dispatchClaim` and asserts the loop rejects — unknown dispatch errors MUST keep throwing after S4 (consistent with q2). S4's dispatch branch must only catch the classifier-positive set.
- **Test seams to reuse:** `stubClient` / `fakeHarness` / `localRepo` / `loopConfig` helpers and the `waitFor` polling helper in `runner/daemon.test.js`; `stubFetch` + `ok`/`fail` helpers in `runner/client.test.js`.
- **Test registration:** `scripts/run-tests.mjs` "Unit Tests (runner)" (~lines 460–491) names every `runner/*.test.js` explicitly, and `tests/run-tests.test.mjs` pins that every suite file on disk is registered — a new `runner/client.backendOutage.test.js` must be added to that list or the gate fails.
- **Evidence gap (does not block):** the cited source-research folder `docs/tasks/2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4/` (`RESPONSE.md` S4, `WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md` Cause 4, `TDD-TEST-EXAMPLES.md`, `GUIDE-04-backend-unreachable-502.md`, `RESPONSE_SURVEY.md` q5) is absent from this checkout (verified: no such folder; repo-wide search for `backend-unreachable|WIDE_NET|Backend 502` finds nothing). The GUIDE-04 §2/§3 test shapes are therefore reconstructed from the stage brief plus the in-repo client shapes above; Step 0 re-derives the exact 502/dropped-socket fixtures from `runner/client.js` and Node fetch behavior rather than trusting the brief's prose. If the folder exists upstream, pull it in Step 0 and reconcile (shapes should match; any conflict is resolved in favor of the observed client behavior).

## Key Decisions

1. **Explicit non-fatal enumeration, never an inverted catch-all (survey q2).** One `isTransientBackendError(err)` predicate owns the set: `statusCode ∈ {502, 503, 504}` OR a network-layer failure (fetch rejection: `TypeError: fetch failed`, `ECONNREFUSED`/`ECONNRESET`/`ETIMEDOUT`/`EAI_AGAIN`/socket-hangup causes — exact list fixed in Step 0 from observed shapes). Everything else falls through to today's generic path. New failure modes stay loud by construction.
2. **Classifier lives next to the client, used by the daemon.** Recommended: export from `runner/client.js` (it defines the error shapes) and import in `runner/daemon.js`. Rejected: duplicating status checks at each catch site (drifts), or putting it in `shared/` (runner-only concern; no backend/wire change).
3. **In-assignment branch = interrupt-with-reason + return, copying `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED`.** Return shape `{ interrupted: true, executionId, epoch, reason, transient: true }` so the loop (and logs) can distinguish outage ride-through from other interrupts. The `transient` flag is additive and internal-only.
4. **`executeIntegrationAssignment` gets the same branch (parity).** Same classifier, same interrupt+return shape. Cost is a few lines; leaving it out would keep "backend restart kills an integrate job's process" as a known hole. (Single-shot mode still ends the process either way — see Decision 6.)
5. **Idle loop: bounded retries with backoff on idempotent calls (survey q3), minimum sleep-and-continue.** `dispatchClaim` classifier-positive errors: retry up to N (recommended 3) with growing waits (recommended 1s→2s→4s, capped at `pollMs`), then keep waiting (back off one `pollMs` and re-poll) without consuming idle budget and without exiting — mirroring the existing 429/`RUNNER_PAUSED` branches (lines 2980–2997). Join-time (`joinAndHeartbeat`) transient failures: add the same bounded retry at startup only if the Step 0 probe confirms join is a live crash path during outages; otherwise document as a follow-up, not scope creep.
6. **Fatal set unchanged: `STALE_EPOCH`, auth/credential failures, unknown errors.** `STALE_EPOCH` keeps propagating in all three catches (epoch fencing). Auth failures (401/credential rejection) exit loud — retrying them would spin forever on a revoked credential. Unknown errors keep the generic interrupt+rethrow path (and the `persistent-loop-probe` test keeps passing unmodified). `runSingleAssignment` keeps its non-zero-exit contract: a transient-interrupted result there maps to a clean non-zero exit with the reason (the process must end anyway with no loop to continue; the win is the task is released WITH a reason instead of crashing). Confirm this mapping in Open Questions if CI callers need `interrupted:true` to read as success.
7. **One-line log per ride-through (survey q4).** `logger.warn` (or `logger.error` where the sibling branches use it — match the `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` sink) naming cause + `projectId/taskId`; retry attempts stay quiet (or debug-level) so a 37s outage window does not spam the journal.

## Steps

### Step 0 — Recon and reproduce (research; no behavior change) — biggest risk, first

- Re-verify all line numbers above on the implementation checkout; confirm the db49 loop catch is present and that `dispatchClaim` line ~3018 is still the idle crash path.
- Confirm fatal-code facts: which `code`/`statusCode` the backend sends for auth/credential rejection (401? `ROTATE_INVALID_STATE`? — read the backend runner-auth path) so the classifier provably excludes them; confirm `STALE_EPOCH` surfaces as `code` on 409 (already pinned by `client.test.js`).
- Derive the exact dropped-socket shapes: stub `fetchImpl` to reject the way Node fetch does on refused/reset connections and record `{ name, message, code, cause }` — these become the classifier's network set and the GUIDE-04 §2 fixtures. Check the Node version in `.node-version`/CI: undici error text differs across versions, so match on stable signals (`code`/`cause.code` + `statusCode` absence), not message substrings alone.
- If reachable, pull the upstream `2e663986-...` folder and reconcile GUIDE-04 §2/§3 shapes with the observed client behavior (observed behavior wins on conflict).
- Write a throwaway repro (under `/tmp`, not committed): stub client whose `complete`/`progress` throws a 502 mid-assignment → run `executeAssignment` (or the loop with `dispatchIdleLimit` bounded) → confirm today's interrupt+rethrow/exit; stub `dispatchClaim` to throw 502 → confirm the loop exits today. This is the red baseline for Steps 2–3.
- Depends on: nothing. Validates: problem statement still accurate; classifier inputs fully enumerated before any branch is written.

### Step 1 — Make the change easy: extract classifier + fixtures (refactor; no behavior change)

- Add and export `isTransientBackendError(err)` in `runner/client.js` (name to match repo conventions at implementation time; MARK/JSDoc comment block per repo style). Pure predicate, no logging, no dependencies.
- Add unit tests for the classifier (in the new `runner/client.backendOutage.test.js` file, or `runner/client.test.js` if that reads better — decide at implementation time; the outage file must exist regardless for Step 4): 502/503/504 (with and without backend `code`), dropped-socket shapes from Step 0, and negatives: `STALE_EPOCH`/409, 401/auth, 429, 500 (deliberately NOT transient — 500 is a backend bug, stays loud), generic `Error`, `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED`.
- Add shared stub fixtures (`fail(502, ...)`, `fetchImpl` rejecting with socket-shape) for daemon tests to reuse.
- Depends on: Step 0. Validates: `node --test runner/client.test.js runner/client.backendOutage.test.js` green; `git diff` shows no behavior change (classifier unreachable from any catch yet).

### Step 2 — Make the change: in-assignment transient branch (interrupt + return)

- In `executeAssignment`'s catch (`runner/daemon.js` ~2296–2453), insert the transient branch after the `failedOutcome` block and before the generic flush/interrupt/rethrow path: `if (isTransientBackendError(err))` → best-effort flush (copy the sibling pattern), best-effort `client.interrupt` WITH the redacted reason (best-effort: the interrupt itself may 502 — swallow, lease TTL bounds it), one-line warn log (survey q4), `return { interrupted: true, executionId, epoch, reason, transient: true }`.
- Same branch in `executeIntegrationAssignment`'s catch (~2655–2697), adapted to its locals (`integrationExecutionId`/`integrationEpoch` untouched; task interrupt uses task `executionId`/`epoch` as the sibling code does).
- Audit `runSingleAssignment`: map a transient-interrupted result to a clean non-zero exit carrying the reason (Decision 6). Keep `STALE_EPOCH` propagation and all other branches byte-identical.
- Depends on: Step 1. Validates: Step 0 repro now returns instead of throwing; new daemon tests (Step 4) fail-before/pass-after.

### Step 3 — Idle loop: transient-aware dispatch polling (bounded retries + backoff)

- In `runDispatchLoop`'s `dispatchClaim` catch (~2976–3020), add a classifier-positive branch before the final `else { throw err }`: bounded retries (recommended: up to 3 attempts, 1s→2s→4s backoff) then — whether retries are exhausted or skipped per the minimum fallback — `polls += 1`, one-line log, `sleep(pollMs)`, `continue` WITHOUT consuming idle budget (same shape as the 429/`RUNNER_PAUSED` branches). Unknown errors still hit `throw err` (the `persistent-loop-probe` test must pass unmodified).
- Verify (no change expected): heartbeat timer and claim-renewal paths already warn-and-continue. Probe join-time: if `joinAndHeartbeat` transient failure is a live crash path, wrap it with the same bounded retry; if the probe shows it is rare/unverifiable, record as a follow-up instead of gold-plating.
- Depends on: Step 1 (Steps 2 and 3 are independent of each other once the classifier exists; sequence 2 before 3 so the in-assignment fix lands first). Validates: stub `dispatchClaim` to 502 twice then succeed → loop survives and processes work; stub it to 502 persistently with bounded `dispatchIdleLimit`... (note: transient backoff must not consume idle budget, so bound this test by polls/success instead of idling out).

### Step 4 — Tests: outage suite + fatality boundary + registration

- Create `runner/client.backendOutage.test.js` (GUIDE-04 §2 reconstructed): 502 shape through the real `createRunnerClient.call` path (stub `fetchImpl` returning `{ ok: false, status: 502 }`), dropped-socket shape (`fetchImpl` rejecting), and recovery (fail N times then succeed → client usable again, no wedged state).
- GUIDE-04 §3 fatality-boundary test (flipped red): drive `executeAssignment` (or the dispatch loop with a one-assignment harness fake, reusing `stubClient`/`fakeHarness`/`loopConfig` from `daemon.test.js`) with a stub backend call throwing transient → assert returned (not rethrown), interrupt carried the reason, loop kept polling; with `STALE_EPOCH` → assert still rethrown (`expect(rethrown).toBe(false)` transient / `toBe(true)` stale-epoch). Place daemon-level tests in `runner/daemon.test.js` beside the existing `runDispatchLoop` block; keep client-level shapes in the outage file.
- Register `runner/client.backendOutage.test.js` in `scripts/run-tests.mjs` "Unit Tests (runner)" args list (alphabetical position beside `runner/client.test.js`).
- Prove red→green: run the new tests against the pre-Step-2/3 code (stash the branches) to confirm they fail, then with the branches to confirm they pass. Record both outputs in the task docs.
- Depends on: Steps 2–3. Validates: `node --test runner/client.backendOutage.test.js runner/daemon.test.js runner/client.test.js` green; `tests/run-tests.test.mjs` registration pin green.

### Step 5 — Docs, hygiene, full gates, and rollout/confirm plan

- Docs: short note in `runner/README.md` if it documents loop failure handling (transient backend errors ride through with interrupt+reason; `STALE_EPOCH`/auth/unknown stay fatal); keep MARK/JSDoc on touched functions accurate. No wire/API doc changes (no contract change).
- Hygiene: `git diff --stat` + grep review — only `runner/client.js`, `runner/daemon.js`, `runner/client.backendOutage.test.js`, `runner/daemon.test.js`, `scripts/run-tests.mjs`, and docs touched. No second catch-restructure: the db49 loop catch stays exactly as-is (verify by diff).
- Full gates: focused files, then `npm test` (root gate incl. the runner suite), plus any lint gate configured for `runner/` (check `package.json` scripts/CI at implementation time).
- Rollout/confirm (post-merge, needs permission — PROD-READ-ONLY): E4 timestamp-join on `db24c124`, `1f8959ca`, `f56e9878`, `ef21e99b`, `bae668cb`; then after rollout, compare runner-journal crash-restart rate across a backend restart window before/after while assignment success holds. Do NOT run these without the permission grant; the implementation is verifiable without them.
- Depends on: Step 4.

## Validation Plan

| Check | Command / evidence | Expected |
|-------|--------------------|----------|
| Classifier unit tests | `node --test runner/client.backendOutage.test.js` (classifier block) | Transient positives pass; `STALE_EPOCH`/401/429/500/generic negatives pass |
| Outage shapes (GUIDE-04 §2) | Same file (502 shape, dropped-socket shape, recovery) | Fail-before / pass-after recorded |
| Fatality boundary (GUIDE-04 §3) | `node --test runner/daemon.test.js` (new boundary tests) | Transient returns + interrupt-with-reason + loop polls on; stale-epoch rethrows |
| No-regression on unknown | `node --test runner/daemon.test.js` (`persistent-loop-probe` test) | Passes unmodified — unknown dispatch errors still throw |
| Focused client tests | `node --test runner/client.test.js` | All pass (classifier export does not disturb existing shapes) |
| Registration pin | `node --test tests/run-tests.test.mjs` (or via `npm test`) | Green with the new suite file listed |
| Full unit gate | `npm test` | Green (runner suite included via `scripts/run-tests.mjs`) |
| Scope audit | `git diff --stat` + grep `isTransientBackendError` in `runner/` | Only the files listed in Step 5; db49 loop catch untouched |
| Manual repro | `/tmp` script from Step 0 re-run post-fix | Mid-assignment 502 → interrupt+return; dispatch 502s → backoff + re-poll, no exit |
| Prod confirm (needs permission) | E4 timestamp-join; journal crash-restart rate vs assignment success | Restart rate drops across backend windows; success holds |

Highest-risk validation: the Step 4 daemon boundary tests — `runDispatchLoop` is poll-driven, so bound the loop deterministically with the existing `stubClient`/`loopConfig({ dispatchPollMs: 1, dispatchIdleLimit })` seams (never wall-clock sleeps); follow the existing `runDispatchLoop` tests' count-then-succeed stub pattern.

## Risks

- **Over-matching the classifier (q2 trade-off):** an over-broad network set could swallow an auth or fencing failure and spin instead of exiting loud. Mitigation: allowlist only `502/503/504` + observed socket shapes; explicit negative tests for 401/`STALE_EPOCH`/429/500; match on stable `code`/`statusCode`, not message substrings.
- **Under-matching on undici version drift:** fetch-failure text varies by Node version. Mitigation: Step 0 derives shapes on the repo's pinned Node; predicate prefers `cause.code`/absence-of-`statusCode` signals.
- **Poison-task flap:** after S4, a persistently-502ing backend call re-queues the task each attempt (runner survives, task flaps until the backend heals). Strictly better than a restart storm; consecutive-failure backoff is out of scope (see Non-goals).
- **Interrupt-during-outage is best-effort by necessity:** the ride-through interrupt itself may 502; the lease TTL is the backstop (same as every sibling branch). The one-line log preserves discoverability.
- **Missing source research:** GUIDE-04 §2/§3 shapes are reconstructed (see Evidence gap). Mitigation: shapes are re-derived from the observed client code in Step 0; reconcile with upstream docs if they surface.

## Non-goals

- Any change to the db49d6c6 loop-level catch (it stays exactly as-is) or to `interrupt` → `complete(failed)` routing for generic errors.
- Retrying non-idempotent calls (`complete`, `interrupt` stay single-attempt best-effort); retries apply only to idempotent idle calls (dispatch poll, and join/heartbeat only per Step 3's probe).
- Consecutive-failure backoff/circuit-breaking for flapping tasks; treating HTTP 500 as transient.
- `--no-verify`, worktree, hook, or systemd unit changes.
- Running the PROD-READ-ONLY E4 timestamp-join or journal analysis without the permission grant.

## Open Questions

1. **Survey confirmation:** `SURVEY.md` answers are empty — confirm the four adopted recommended options (q1 stay-alive+report, q2 transient-only survival, q3 bounded backoff retries, q4 one-line log). If q3's simpler "just wait and re-check" is preferred, Step 3 collapses to the sleep-and-continue minimum with no retry counter. (Default if unanswered: proceed as planned.)
2. **Single-shot mapping (Decision 6):** confirm transient-interrupted in `runSingleAssignment` should exit non-zero with the reason (recommended, preserves the CI contract) rather than exit 0. If 0 is required, Step 2 skips the mapping.
3. **Retry budget (Decision 5):** confirm 3 attempts / 1s→2s→4s backoff for dispatch-poll retries, or name other bounds. Any reasonable bound fits the same code shape.
4. None other — all technical facts above were verified in-repo this session except the noted source-folder gap.

## Work estimate / sequencing note

Big/research pieces first per the stage brief: Step 0 (chain verification + exact error-shape derivation + upstream doc reconcile) and the Step 3 join-time probe are the riskiest and come before/around the small behavior edits. Steps 1–3 are small and mechanical once the classifier set is fixed. Total: 5 implementation steps + gates, all in `runner/client.js`, `runner/daemon.js`, `runner/client.backendOutage.test.js`, `runner/daemon.test.js`, `scripts/run-tests.mjs`, plus a short `runner/README.md` note and the post-rollout confirm (permission-gated).

Task: `78eac844-250a-44d1-810e-6f047eb5a59e`. Branch `kb/78eac844-250a-44d1-810e-6f047eb5a59e` vs `main`.

STALE_EPOCH propagation untouched at all three sites (lines 2369, 2752, 3283).

Tests re-run in this review, all green:

- `node --test runner/client.backendOutage.test.js` → 9 pass / 0 fail

Known minor duplication (6-line cause-walk mirrored in `describeBackendOutageCause`) is self-flagged in comments and semantically distinct (first-found vs recognized code) — not debt worth blocking on. `isTransientBackendError(err)` positional predicate matches existing repo predicate convention.

reports.content:
# Upgrade-safety review — S4 branch (0.2.0 -> 0.2.1)

Task: `78eac844-250a-44d1-810e-6f047eb5a59e`. Stage asks to confirm, without fixing, that the current implementation will not break existing installs on update, and to FAIL if it would.

Verdict: **PASS** — no update-breaking change found. Evidence below is from reading the branch diff against `main` (`git diff $(git merge-base HEAD main)..HEAD`) and the update/install code paths. This stage is docs-only; no source was modified.

## What the branch changes

Runtime code is runner-only and small:

- `runner/client.js`: adds `TRANSIENT_BACKEND_STATUSES`, `TRANSIENT_NETWORK_CODES`, and the pure predicate `isTransientBackendError(err)`. The existing `createRunnerClient.call` path is untouched.
- `runner/daemon.js`: imports `isTransientBackendError`; adds `retryTransient`, `describeBackendOutageCause`; adds transient branches to `joinAndHeartbeat` (register + heartbeat retries), `executeAssignment`, `executeIntegrationAssignment`, `runDispatchLoop` (dispatch-poll retry/backoff), and `runSingleAssignment` (maps transient-interrupted to a clean non-zero exit).
- `runner/version.json`: `0.2.0` -> `0.2.1`. `apiVersion` stays `1.0.0`; `requires.backendApi` stays `>=1.0.0 <2.0.0`.
- `runner/README.md`: docs only.
- `scripts/run-tests.mjs` + `publish.sh`: register `runner/client.backendOutage.test.js` in the runner gates.
- `runner/client.backendOutage.test.js` + `runner/daemon.test.js`: new regression tests.

Nothing else runtime touches config, credentials, state, systemd, or packaging logic. No new dependencies, no new env flags, no schema or wire changes (the `interrupt` `reason` field already exists; `transient` is an in-memory flag on the return object only).

## Upgrade paths checked

### Self-update channel (`runner/updates/index.js`, `runner/updates/state.js`, `runner/main.js`)

- `filterReleaseCandidate` requires strictly newer + not prerelease + backend-compatible + platform asset. `0.2.1` is strictly newer semver, final (not prerelease), same `requires.backendApi` range, and ships for the same linux/darwin x64/arm64 assets via the same `packageRunner`. Old `0.2.0` installs are offered `0.2.1`; no downgrade is ever selected (never-downgrade rule intact).
- `applyUpdate` downloads, re-verifies sha256, extracts to `releases/<v>/unpacked`, normalizes the tar top-dir, sanity-checks `version.json`, carries `api/node_modules` over from the previous tree, then atomically flips `current`/`previous` symlinks. This branch modifies none of that logic, so atomicity and lock behavior are unchanged.
- `bootstrapUpdateState` (called first in `main.js`) still rolls back after 3 failed boots by flipping `current` back to `previous`. `markUpdateSuccess` still gates GC on first good heartbeat. Both operate on `update-state.json` whose shape this branch does not change (`status`/`bootAttempts`/`from`/`to` — see `runner/updates/state.js`). `0.2.0` reads a `0.2.1`-written state file identically; rollback to the `0.2.0` tree is byte-safe.

### Backend gating (`api/flow/runnerVersionCompat.js`, `api/version.json`, `runner/version.json`)

- Backend `accepts.runner` is `>=1.0.0 <2.0.0`; runner `requires.backendApi` is the same range. Component compatibility is unchanged.
- Backend floors are `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION=0.1.0` and `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION=0.1.0` (`.env.example`). `0.2.0` and `0.2.1` are both well above the minimum, so neither trips `RUNNER_VERSION_BELOW_MINIMUM`, and `0.2.1` does not newly show as below-recommended. Advertising `runnerVersion 0.2.1` in `factsFor` is a display/matrix change only.

### Fresh install and manual tarball (`scripts/package-runner.mjs`, `runner/bin/kainbain-runner`, `scripts/install-local-runner.sh`)

- `packageRunner` copies `runner/`, `shared/`, `api/` with pruning of `*.test.js`/`*.spec.js` (see `copyPruned`/`assertClean`), so the new `runner/client.backendOutage.test.js` never ships. `INSTALL.txt` and the leg-closure (`RUNNER_LEG_BUNDLED_DEPS`) are untouched; no new bare imports were added (`daemon.js` -> `./client.js` is a relative import present in every bundle).
- The `kainbain-runner` wrapper resolves `current` on every boot and reboots on symlink flip or the `restart-requested` sentinel. The new transient paths write neither, so wrapper restart semantics are unchanged (the daemon simply stays running during an outage instead of exiting — the intended S4 behavior, not a break).
- `install-local-runner.sh` writes the same env file and systemd unit keys (`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_*`); no env keys are added, removed, or renamed, and `runner/config.js` is not in the diff.

### Wire protocol

- `runner/client.js` `call` still sends identical paths/bodies/headers and still throws `{statusCode, code}` on non-2xx. The new predicate only reads `statusCode`/`code`/`cause.code`; it changes no request bytes.
- `interrupt` reasoning reuses the existing `reason` string field (capped 500). The transient branches use a new reason prefix (`Backend unreachable mid-assignment: ...`), which the backend records as an opaque history string (`api/flow/executionLedger.js` interrupt path) — nothing parses the prefix. `complete` gains no new fields. A `0.2.1` runner talks to any `1.0.0` backend exactly as `0.2.0` did; no paired backend upgrade is required.

## Per-dimension breakage analysis

| Dimension | Finding | Breaks existing install? |
|---|---|---|
| Version / updater | Strictly newer final `0.2.1`, same compat range, same assets; satisfies `check-runner-version-bump` (runner code changed + version bumped). | No |
| Backend floor | Both versions above `MIN 0.1.0`; no refusal, no forced update. | No |
| Wire / backend API | No endpoint, method, or body-shape change; `reason` text only. | No |
| Config / env / credential | `config.js` untouched; no new required vars; `credentialFile.js` untouched; `~/.kainbain/runner-<short>.credential` format unchanged. | No |
| State files (`update-state.json`, workdir) | No schema change, no migration, no new persisted fields; worktree reaping unchanged. | No |
| Node / runtime | Only long-supported syntax (`Set`, `Number.isFinite`, optional chaining — already used in these files); no new npm deps or native modules. | No |
| Bundle layout | No new runtime files; edited files ship together in one tarball so `daemon.js` -> `./client.js` always resolves. | No |
| Boot: `register`/`heartbeat` retries | Bounded `[250,500,1000]` attempts on classifier-positive errors only, then the original throw. Adds at most ~1.75s before boot failure on a long outage; auth/unknown still exit loud immediately. Strictly more tolerant than today. | No |
| Idle: dispatch-poll retry | `[1000,2000,4000]` capped to `pollMs`, then `polls+=1` + `sleep(pollMs)` + `continue` without consuming idle budget (same shape as the existing `429`/`RUNNER_PAUSED` branches). Unknown errors still hit `throw err` (`persistent-loop-probe` test unmodified). Process stays alive through a long outage instead of systemd-restarting — intended behavior, polls resume on heal. | No (intended liveness change, not a brick) |
| In-assignment: `executeAssignment`/`executeIntegrationAssignment` | Transient -> best-effort `interrupt` with reason + `return {interrupted:true,...,transient:true}` instead of rethrow. The interrupt itself is swallowed if it also 502s (lease TTL is the backstop, same as sibling branches). Task is released via the identical re-queue path as before. | No |
| Single-shot: `runSingleAssignment` | Transient-interrupted maps to `throw new Error(reason)` (non-zero exit preserved), matching the pre-existing non-zero contract where the raw backend error used to propagate. Error *text* changes from e.g. `Backend 502 on ...` to `Backend unreachable mid-assignment: ...`; CI callers branching on the old exact string would see a different message but still a failure exit. Not an install break. | No |
| Logging | One warn/error line per ride-through naming cause + ids; retries stay quiet. No log-volume contract break. | No |
| Rollback | `previous` still points at the `0.2.0` tree; state is symmetric; manual/rollback flip restores byte-identical old code. | No |
| Tests / gates (`run-tests.mjs`, `publish.sh`) | Both lists now name `runner/client.backendOutage.test.js`; nothing here runs inside already-installed trees. (Prior CI failure in `tests/publish.test.mjs` was a list-pin mismatch at that time; the branch's `publish.sh` update aligns the lists — a gate-strictness item for the next CI run, not an install-safety issue.) | No |

## Deliberate-shape checks (why these cannot brick installs)

- **Classifier is allowlist-only.** `statusCode` present -> transient iff in `{502,503,504}`; otherwise the cause chain (depth 4) must carry a known `ECONN*`/`UND_ERR_*` code. `STALE_EPOCH`/409, 401/403 auth, 429, 500, and unknown errors all return `false` by construction, so new failure modes stay loud instead of spinning. A bare `TypeError: fetch failed` with no recognized code (e.g. misconfigured `backendUrl`) also returns `false` — ambiguous failures keep exiting loud.
- **No persistence drift.** The outage cause helper (`describeBackendOutageCause`) is pure string building with `redactSecretsText`; nothing new is written to disk.
- **Bounded by construction.** Both retry loops are capped arrays; the idle path always sleeps `pollMs` and re-polls, so a dead backend cannot create a hot loop (same backoff shape as the pre-existing `429` branch).
- **db49d6c6 not reworked.** The loop-level catch around `executeAssignment` is untouched by this diff; S4 only adds branches inside the assignment catches and the dispatch-poll catch, per the plan constraint.

## What was verified

- `git diff $(git merge-base HEAD main)..HEAD` file list and full diff of `runner/client.js`, `runner/daemon.js`, `runner/version.json`, `scripts/run-tests.mjs`, `publish.sh`, `runner/README.md`.
- `runner/updates/{index,manifest,state}.js`, `runner/main.js`, `runner/credentialFile.js`, `runner/config.js`, `scripts/package-runner.mjs`, `runner/bin/kainbain-runner`, `api/flow/runnerVersionCompat.js`, `api/version.json`, `.env.example` version knobs — all confirming no gating, schema, or contract change.
- `runner/daemon.test.js` added tests assert single-shot still exits non-zero on transient, unknown dispatch errors still throw, and `STALE_EPOCH` still propagates (boundary pinned). No existing test assertions were rewritten to hide a contract change (diff is additive in `daemon.test.js`).

Not executed beyond reads in this stage (docs-only): no test runs, no tariff/install simulation, no journal check. That is CI/rollout work; it does not affect the install-safety conclusion because the updater/packaging/state paths involved are fully readable and unchanged.

## Conclusion

The current `0.2.1` implementation is a backward-compatible, runner-only patch: same backend range, same config/credential/state contracts, same bundle shape, bounded retries, unchanged audit of fatal paths, and clean rollback. Existing installs can update in place via the self-update channel, fresh installs extract the same layout, and a failed `0.2.1` boot still rolls back to `0.2.0`. Nothing in the diff requires a paired backend upgrade, env-file rewrite, credential re-collection, or manual intervention.

#!/bin/bash
# kainbain-runner — supported entrypoint for a self-updating Runner install.
#
# Layout (see runner/updates/state.js):
#   $RUNNER_INSTALL_ROOT/
#     releases/<version>/unpacked/   versioned trees (current + previous kept)
#     current -> releases/<v>/unpacked
#     previous -> releases/<v-1>/unpacked
#     update-state.json
#
# The wrapper resolves `current` on every (re)start, so an in-place update
# that flips the symlink takes effect on the next boot. A restart happens
# when the run actually staged an update (the `current` target changed
# while the daemon ran), or when the daemon left a `restart-requested`
# sentinel beside the install root (operator Restart: reboot the SAME tree
# on its current version, no update involved). A normal completion —
# single assignment done, or dispatch idle-out — exits 0 with `current`
# untouched and no sentinel, and the wrapper stops instead of re-running
# finished work. Any non-zero code stops the loop and propagates the
# failure.
set -u

INSTALL_ROOT="${KAINBAIN_RUNNER_INSTALL_ROOT:-$HOME/.kainbain/runner-install}"
ENTRY="runner/main.js"

# doctor — read-only install health report (migration pre-check + "says out
# of date" triage). Prints the effective install root, current/previous
# targets, installed version, update state, and one block per
# kainbain-runner-*.service unit (entrypoint kind, unit version, update env,
# backend record). NEVER writes: no reloads, no restarts, no state changes.
# Exit 0 when the install is structurally sound, 1 when something needs
# attention (direct node main.js entrypoint, missing current link, unknown
# version, rolled-back state). A backend that is unreachable, or a runner
# that is merely behind the desired version, is REPORTED but keeps exit 0 —
# those are network/release states, not install damage.
doctor_tree_version() {
	# $1 = tree dir. Release trees carry version.json at the root;
	# legacy/dev trees carry it under runner/.

#!/bin/bash
# kainbain-runner — supported entrypoint for a self-updating Runner install.

#     releases/<version>/unpacked/   versioned trees (current + previous kept)
#     current -> releases/<v>/unpacked
#     previous -> releases/<v-1>/unpacked
#     update-state.json
#
# The wrapper resolves `current` on every (re)start, so an in-place update
# that flips the symlink takes effect on the next boot. A restart happens
# when the run actually staged an update (the `current` target changed
# while the daemon ran), or when the daemon left a `restart-requested`
# sentinel beside the install root (operator Restart: reboot the SAME tree
# on its current version, no update involved). A normal completion —
# single assignment done, or dispatch idle-out — exits 0 with `current`
# untouched and no sentinel, and the wrapper stops instead of re-running
# finished work. Any non-zero code stops the loop and propagates the
# failure.
set -u

INSTALL_ROOT="${KAINBAIN_RUNNER_INSTALL_ROOT:-$HOME/.kainbain/runner-install}"
ENTRY="runner/main.js"

# doctor — read-only install health report (migration pre-check + "says out
# of date" triage). Prints the effective install root, current/previous
# targets, installed version, update state, and one block per
# kainbain-runner-*.service unit (entrypoint kind, unit version, update env,
# backend record). NEVER writes: no reloads, no restarts, no state changes.
# Exit 0 when the install is structurally sound, 1 when something needs
# attention (direct node main.js entrypoint, missing current link, unknown
# version, rolled-back state). A backend that is unreachable, or a runner
# that is merely behind the desired version, is REPORTED but keeps exit 0 —
# those are network/release states, not install damage.
doctor_tree_version() {
	# $1 = tree dir. Release trees carry version.json at the root;
	# legacy/dev trees carry it under runner/.
	for _f in "$1/version.json" "$1/runner/version.json"; do
		if [ -f "$_f" ] && command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then
			_v="$(node -e 'const v=JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync(process.argv[1],"utf8")).runnerVersion;if(typeof v!=="string"||!v)process.exit(1);console.log(v);' "$_f" 2>/dev/null)" || continue
			[ -n "$_v" ] && { printf '%s' "$_v"; return 0; }
		fi
	done
	return 1
}

doctor_env_val() {
	# $1 = env file, $2 = key. Parsed, never sourced (values are only read).
	[ -f "$1" ] || return 1

}

doctor_backend_record() {

	_backend="$1"; _id="$2"

			.then((r) => { if (!r.ok) throw new Error("HTTP " + r.status); return r.json(); })

	_unit_filter=""

			--unit=*) _unit_filter="${1#--unit=}"; shift ;;

#!/bin/bash
# kainbain-runner — supported entrypoint for a self-updating Runner install.
#
# Layout (see runner/updates/state.js):
#   $RUNNER_INSTALL_ROOT/
#     releases/<version>/unpacked/   versioned trees (current + previous kept)
#     current -> releases/<v>/unpacked
#     previous -> releases/<v-1>/unpacked
#     update-state.json
#
# The wrapper resolves `current` on every (re)start, so an in-place update
# that flips the symlink takes effect on the next boot. A restart happens
# when the run actually staged an update (the `current` target changed
# while the daemon ran), or when the daemon left a `restart-requested`
# sentinel beside the install root (operator Restart: reboot the SAME tree
# on its current version, no update involved). A normal completion —
# single assignment done, or dispatch idle-out — exits 0 with `current`
# untouched and no sentinel, and the wrapper stops instead of re-running
# finished work. Any non-zero code stops the loop and propagates the
# failure.
set -u

INSTALL_ROOT="${KAINBAIN_RUNNER_INSTALL_ROOT:-$HOME/.kainbain/runner-install}"
ENTRY="runner/main.js"

# doctor — read-only install health report (migration pre-check + "says out
# of date" triage). Prints the effective install root, current/previous
# targets, installed version, update state, and one block per
# kainbain-runner-*.service unit (entrypoint kind, unit version, update env,
# backend record). NEVER writes: no reloads, no restarts, no state changes.
# Exit 0 when the install is structurally sound, 1 when something needs
# attention (direct node main.js entrypoint, missing current link, unknown
# version, rolled-back state). A backend that is unreachable, or a runner
# that is merely behind the desired version, is REPORTED but keeps exit 0 —
# those are network/release states, not install damage.
doctor_tree_version() {
	# $1 = tree dir. Release trees carry version.json at the root;
	# legacy/dev trees carry it under runner/.
	for _f in "$1/version.json" "$1/runner/version.json"; do
		if [ -f "$_f" ] && command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then
			_v="$(node -e 'const v=JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync(process.argv[1],"utf8")).runnerVersion;if(typeof v!=="string"||!v)process.exit(1);console.log(v);' "$_f" 2>/dev/null)" || continue
			[ -n "$_v" ] && { printf '%s' "$_v"; return 0; }
		fi
	done
	return 1
}

doctor_env_val() {
	# $1 = env file, $2 = key. Parsed, never sourced (values are only read).
	[ -f "$1" ] || return 1
	grep -m1 "^$2=" "$1" 2>/dev/null | cut -d= -f2- | sed -e 's/^"//' -e 's/"$//' -e "s/^'//" -e "s/'$//"
}

doctor_backend_record() {
	# $1 = backend base URL, $2 = runner id. One line on stdout, always.
	_backend="$1"; _id="$2"
	if [ -z "$_backend" ] || [ -z "$_id" ]; then
		echo "backend: (unknown — no backend URL or runner id configured)"
		return 0
	fi
	if ! command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then
		echo "backend: (unknown — node not on PATH)"
		return 0
	fi
	node -e '
		const [base, id] = process.argv.slice(1);
		fetch(base.replace(/\/+$/, "") + "/runners", { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(10000) })
			.then((r) => { if (!r.ok) throw new Error("HTTP " + r.status); return r.json(); })
			.then((list) => {
				const rec = (Array.isArray(list) ? list : []).find((x) => x && x.runnerId === id);
				if (!rec) { console.log("backend: reachable (" + base + ") — runner " + id + " not registered"); return; }
				const st = rec.updateStatus ? rec.updateStatus.state + (rec.updateStatus.reason ? ": " + rec.updateStatus.reason : "") : "(none)";
				console.log("backend: reachable (" + base + ") reported=" + (rec.runnerVersion || "?")
					+ " desired=" + (rec.recommendedVersion || "?") + " minimum=" + (rec.minimumVersion || "?")
					+ " update_available=" + rec.updateAvailable + " below_minimum=" + rec.belowMinimum
					+ " update_status=" + st);
			})
			.catch((e) => console.log("backend: unreachable (" + base + ": " + (e.cause?.message || e.message) + ")"));
	' "$_backend" "$_id" 2>/dev/null || echo "backend: unreachable ($_backend)"
}

doctor() {
	_unit_filter=""
	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
		case "$1" in
			--unit) _unit_filter="${2:?doctor --unit needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
			--unit=*) _unit_filter="${1#--unit=}"; shift ;;
			*) echo "kainbain-runner doctor: unknown arg '$1' (usage: doctor [--unit NAME])" >&2; return 2 ;;
		esac
	done
	_attention=0
	attention() { _attention=1; echo "attention: $*"; }
	_root="${KAINBAIN_RUNNER_INSTALL_ROOT:-$HOME/.kainbain/runner-install}"
	echo "install_root: $_root"
	if [ -L "$_root/current" ]; then
		_cur="$(readlink "$_root/current")"
		echo "current: $_cur"
	else
		_cur=""
		echo "current: (missing)"
		attention "current symlink missing under $_root — nothing can boot from this install root"
	fi
	if [ -L "$_root/previous" ]; then
		echo "previous: $(readlink "$_root/previous")"
	else
		echo "previous: (none)"
	fi
	if [ -n "$_cur" ] && _installed="$(doctor_tree_version "$_cur" 2>/dev/null)"; then
		echo "installed_version: $_installed"
	else
		echo "installed_version: (unknown)"
		attention "installed version unknown — no readable version.json under the current target"
	fi
	if [ -f "$_root/update-state.json" ]; then
		_state="$(node -e 'const s=JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync(process.argv[1],"utf8"));console.log("status="+(s.status||"?")+" to="+(s.to||s.version||"-")+" attempts="+(s.bootAttempts||0)+" at="+(s.updatedAt||"?"));' "$_root/update-state.json" 2>/dev/null || echo "(unreadable)")"
		echo "update_state: $_state"
		case "$_state" in
			status=rolled-back*) attention "last update rolled back after failed boots — see the runner-update runbook before retrying" ;;
		esac
	else

# Implementation Plan — `--no-verify` for `kb-recovery/*` snapshots + per-task daemon containment

Task: `db49d6c6-bdd5-4600-aaea-15a71042ae20`
Source problem: runner `git commit` without `--no-verify` on internal recovery branches; uncaught worktree-setup error crashes the runner into a systemd restart loop.
Survey input: [SURVEY.md](./SURVEY.md) (Round 1; `answers: {}` — unanswered, so the recommended options below are carried as assumptions pending confirmation).

## Goal

1. Internal `kb-recovery/*` snapshot commits in `runner/project.js` (both the reuse path and the eviction path) pass `--no-verify`, so repo `pre-commit` hooks (binary-guard, linters, formatters) can never block parking unpushed residue.
2. Worktree setup/recovery errors in the runner daemon are contained per-task: the task is failed/released cleanly and the daemon keeps polling instead of exiting 1 into a systemd restart loop.
3. Regression tests in `runner/project.test.js` prove dirty worktrees with a failing `pre-commit` hook still park cleanly onto `kb-recovery/*` via both reuse and eviction.

## Success Criteria

- Both recovery commits (`recovery: unpushed work from reused worktree (…)` in `refreshWorktreeToRemote`, `runner/project.js` ~line 789; `recovery: unpushed work parked before eviction (…)` in `preserveEvictedWorkdir`, `runner/project.js` ~line 466) succeed with a deliberately failing `pre-commit` hook installed, and the parked content is verifiable on the `kb-recovery/*` branch.
- A `prepareWorkdir`/recovery throw inside one assignment no longer terminates `runDispatchLoop`: the loop logs, releases the task, and continues to the next poll. No new crash path is introduced for `runSingleAssignment` (single-shot mode must still exit non-zero on failure so callers/CI see it).
- `node --test runner/project.test.js runner/daemon.test.js` passes, and the repo's unit gate (`npm test`, which runs the `runner` suite via `scripts/run-tests.mjs`) passes.
- Normal (non-recovery) runner commits — e.g. harness wrap-up commits on the task branch — still run hooks unchanged.

## Survey decisions (factored in)

`SURVEY.md` Round 1 asked three questions; all are unanswered (`"answers": {}`). This plan adopts the recommended option for each as a working assumption (flagged for confirmation in Open Questions):

| # | Question | Adopted (recommended) answer | Plan effect |
|---|----------|------------------------------|-------------|
| q1 | Skip checks for emergency backups? | Yes — emergency backups only | `--no-verify` applies ONLY to the two `kb-recovery/*` snapshot commits, never to task-branch or integration commits. |
| q2 | What to do with the one failed task? | Mark failed, move to next task | Contain per-task and keep polling. Refinement: keep the existing `interrupt` (release/re-queue) routing for generic errors rather than `complete(failed)` — see Key Decision 2 for why. Runner survival is the requirement; routing stays as-is. |
| q3 | Visibility of skipped checks? | Clear warning in logs | Emit a `logger.warn` naming the recovery branch and stating hooks were bypassed, at each snapshot commit. |

## Approach

Follow "make the change easy, then make the change":

1. **Easy first:** extract the two near-identical inline recovery-commit blocks into one shared helper (single home for identity flags, message, `--no-verify`, and the warn log), with zero behavior change; add a shared failing-hook test fixture. Land this refactor green before touching behavior.
2. **Then the change:** one-line behavior change inside the helper (`--no-verify` + warn log), plus the two regression tests.
3. **Then containment:** a loop-level `try/catch` around the `executeAssignment` call in `runDispatchLoop` (the proven crash path — see Evidence), with a daemon test; deliberately NOT by removing the rethrow inside `executeAssignment`, which single-shot mode depends on.

No new dependencies, no new config flags, no schema/wire changes.

## Evidence (what the research established)

- **Commit sites:** `runner/project.js` `preserveEvictedWorkdir` (~line 463–467) and `refreshWorktreeToRemote` (~line 786–790) both run `git commit` with `-c user.name/email` but no `--no-verify`. A hook failure surfaces as `RunnerGitError(code: "git-failed")` via `runGit`.
- **Crash path:** `executeAssignment` (`runner/daemon.js` ~line 2243–2333) catches generic errors, best-effort `client.interrupt`s, then **rethrows** (line 2332). `runDispatchLoop` awaits `executeAssignment` (line 2928) with **no `try/catch`**, and the loop body has only `try/finally` — so the throw escapes `runLoop` → `main()` (`runner/main.js`) rejects → process exits 1 → systemd restarts → the interrupted task re-queues and the same poisoned worktree is reclaimed → observed 10,776-restart loop. The `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` precedent (interrupt + return, lines 2246–2262) shows the codebase's own pattern for "infra problem, don't die".
- **Hook mechanics:** `scripts/githooks/pre-commit` is the binary guard; `core.hooksPath=scripts/githooks` is set repo-wide and inherited by linked `kb-*` worktrees (existing test at `runner/project.test.js` ~line 364 proves inheritance). So a corrupt PNG staged anywhere in a reused/evicted worktree deterministically aborts both recovery commits today.
- **Test patterns to reuse:** `originWithWorktree()` + `refreshWorktreeToRemote` reuse test (~line 73), eviction parking test (~line 525), staged-index regression test (~line 731), `localRepo()` helper (~line 27). New tests mirror these with a failing hook installed.
- **Test entrypoints:** focused — `node --test runner/project.test.js`; full unit gate — `npm test` (`scripts/run-tests.mjs`, "Unit Tests (runner)" suite names `runner/*.test.js` explicitly).

## Key Decisions

1. **Scope of `--no-verify`: recovery snapshots only (survey q1).** These commits are local safety snapshots on `kb-recovery/*`, never pushed as task output and never merged; hook value there is zero and hook cost is a wedged runner. All other runner-authored commits keep hooks. Rejected: `--no-verify` everywhere (loses the binary-guard backstop on real output), and deleting/disabling repo hooks (mutates user repos).
2. **Containment via loop-level catch, keeping `interrupt` routing (survey q2, refined).** The minimal correct fix is `try/catch` around `await executeAssignment(...)` in `runDispatchLoop`: log the error, continue polling. The task is already released by the `interrupt` inside `executeAssignment`'s catch, satisfying "failing/releasing the task cleanly". Changing generic errors to `complete(outcome: failed)` instead would newly fail tasks for transient infra blips (network, lock contention) — a behavior change far beyond this task — so routing is left untouched. Rejected: removing the rethrow in `executeAssignment` (breaks `runSingleAssignment`'s non-zero-exit contract and the `STALE_EPOCH` contract).
3. **Shared helper over two one-line edits.** Both commit blocks duplicate identity flags and message shape; a `commitRecoverySnapshot(workdir, message, { logger })` helper (name to match repo conventions at implementation time) makes the bypass auditable in one place and prevents future drift between the paths. The helper owns: `-c` identity flags, `--no-verify`, the message, and the q3 warn log.
4. **Failing-hook fixture, not the real binary guard, in tests.** Tests install a trivial `#!/bin/sh; exit 1` hook (via `core.hooksPath` on a fixture dir or a `.git/hooks/pre-commit` file in the temp repo) so they are hermetic, fast, and independent of `check-binary-guard.mjs` internals. One test may additionally exercise the real guard with a corrupt PNG if cheap, but it is not required.

### Step 0 — Recon and reproduce (research; no behavior change)

- Confirm the two commit sites and the `runDispatchLoop` → `executeAssignment` → `prepareWorkdir` → `runGit` throw chain on the current checkout (line numbers above were read this session; re-verify at implementation time).
- Run the existing recovery tests green as a baseline: `node --test runner/project.test.js`.

## What the branch changes

Runtime code is runner-only and small:

- `runner/client.js`: adds `TRANSIENT_BACKEND_STATUSES`, `TRANSIENT_NETWORK_CODES`, and the pure predicate `isTransientBackendError(err)`. The existing `createRunnerClient.call` path is untouched.
- `runner/daemon.js`: imports `isTransientBackendError`; adds `retryTransient`, `describeBackendOutageCause`; adds transient branches to `joinAndHeartbeat` (register + heartbeat retries), `executeAssignment`, `executeIntegrationAssignment`, `runDispatchLoop` (dispatch-poll retry/backoff), and `runSingleAssignment` (maps transient-interrupted to a clean non-zero exit).
- `runner/version.json`: `0.2.0` -> `0.2.1`. `apiVersion` stays `1.0.0`; `requires.backendApi` stays `>=1.0.0 <2.0.0`.
- `runner/README.md`: docs only.
- `scripts/run-tests.mjs` + `publish.sh`: register `runner/client.backendOutage.test.js` in the runner gates.
- `runner/client.backendOutage.test.js` + `runner/daemon.test.js`: new regression tests.

Nothing else runtime touches config, credentials, state, systemd, or packaging logic. No new dependencies, no new env flags, no schema or wire changes (the `interrupt` `reason` field already exists; `transient` is an in-memory flag on the return object only).

## Upgrade paths checked

### Self-update channel (`runner/updates/index.js`, `runner/updates/state.js`, `runner/main.js`)

- `filterReleaseCandidate` requires strictly newer + not prerelease + backend-compatible + platform asset. `0.2.1` is strictly newer semver, final (not prerelease), same `requires.backendApi` range, and ships for the same linux/darwin x64/arm64 assets via the same `packageRunner`. Old `0.2.0` installs are offered `0.2.1`; no downgrade is ever selected (never-downgrade rule intact).
- `applyUpdate` downloads, re-verifies sha256, extracts to `releases/<v>/unpacked`, normalizes the tar top-dir, sanity-checks `version.json`, carries `api/node_modules` over from the previous tree, then atomically flips `current`/`previous` symlinks. This branch modifies none of that logic, so atomicity and lock behavior are unchanged.
- `bootstrapUpdateState` (called first in `main.js`) still rolls back after 3 failed boots by flipping `current` back to `previous`. `markUpdateSuccess` still gates GC on first good heartbeat. Both operate on `update-state.json` whose shape this branch does not change (`status`/`bootAttempts`/`from`/`to` — see `runner/updates/state.js`). `0.2.0` reads a `0.2.1`-written state file identically; rollback to the `0.2.0` tree is byte-safe.

### Backend gating (`api/flow/runnerVersionCompat.js`, `api/version.json`, `runner/version.json`)

- Backend `accepts.runner` is `>=1.0.0 <2.0.0`; runner `requires.backendApi` is the same range. Component compatibility is unchanged.
- Backend floors are `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION=0.1.0` and `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION=0.1.0` (`.env.example`). `0.2.0` and `0.2.1` are both well above the minimum, so neither trips `RUNNER_VERSION_BELOW_MINIMUM`, and `0.2.1` does not newly show as below-recommended. Advertising `runnerVersion 0.2.1` in `factsFor` is a display/matrix change only.

### Fresh install and manual tarball (`scripts/package-runner.mjs`, `runner/bin/kainbain-runner`, `scripts/install-local-runner.sh`)

- `packageRunner` copies `runner/`, `shared/`, `api/` with pruning of `*.test.js`/`*.spec.js` (see `copyPruned`/`assertClean`), so the new `runner/client.backendOutage.test.js` never ships. `INSTALL.txt` and the leg-closure (`RUNNER_LEG_BUNDLED_DEPS`) are untouched; no new bare imports were added (`daemon.js` -> `./client.js` is a relative import present in every bundle).
