meta.output:
Read text file `docs/KB Code Standards.md`.
1|# Values
2|
3|## User understandable over technical language
4|
5|I feel like code should always be understandable by users as they are the ones who dictate process. So the goal of code should make it the most understandable with zero context as possible
6|
7|### Principles
8|
9|- Long variables names where needed to be descriptive
10|- Avoid using technical language such as “factory” or “barrel”
11|- Stick to a common language profile, (tasks always being tasks, stages always being stages etc)
12|- File structure should reflect the call stack
13|- Use of JSDocs to explain variables in pure english
14|- Include why things are done not just what is done
15|- Use a labelled data inport pattern (IE  `({varA , varB}) => {}`)
16|- NEVER MENTION DESIGN PATTERNS
17|- Use @example tags in js doc to easily explain functionality
18|- Every new export also carries a `MARK:` label in the same JSDoc block, sitting directly above the export (only whitespace between `*/` and `export`); `npm run check:jsdoc-example` (<1s) checks this before pushing — copy-paste shapes in docs/agent-docs/KB-Code-Standards.md §Documentation/Jsdoc
19|  
20|  
21|
22|## Functional over Object oreintated
23|
24|Although pure functional code can tend to insanity it is always important to note co-mingle state and functionality. Where possible state should leave in clearly defined places, and functions should show a clear line in how we move from one state to another. Traditional object oriented design mainly serves to gatekeep devs(or for game dev).
25|
26|### Principles
27|
28|- Try and avoid using classes where possible
29|- Currying can be used to create sudo classes, avoid that
30|- Functions should follow black box mentality, clear input delivers the same output with no side affects
31|- Treat variables as immutable unless they are clearly defined states.
32|- Functions should always be named with a verb in, as they are doing something
33|- Give the miniumn data to each function as possible. Pick off fields before invocation.
34|- Each function should only work to achieve its task, with a single responsibility
35|
36|
37|## Co-location over abstraction
38|
39|Although abstraction is an essential part of coding it should always only be done by business level intent, not just on functionality. Ideally if you pick a random file in the codebase you should only need to look at the one folder above it and one folder under it to get all the context on its functionality.
40|
41|### Principles
42|- Unit tests should always be placed next to the relevant file
43|- Generally functions called in a higher function should be placed in a folder of that functions name. IE if `funA.js` calls `funB.js` it should be `./funA/funB.js`
44|- Generic/helper functions should only be made if they are repeatedly doing the same thing.
45|- Helpers should be treated like react state and exist at the lowest level folder that is common in the hierarchy of the folders
46|- If abstracting it would take up more lines/characters than just embedding that line directly on a per file basis avoid doing it. IE don’t abstract a single line just because its repeated unless it has some complex logic like a regex.
47|- Don’t fear repetition of code
48|- Make sure the code is easily searchable for any given task. If I said modify the task history box in the ui it should  be easy and logical to figure out where that is.
49|- Use folders as a tool for organising
50|
51|## Tested over trusted 
52|
53|Functionality should not assumed to exist until it is tested and evidenced. “it should work” isn’t always reliable and we want to make sure there are no regressions. 
54|
55|### Principles
56|- Try and at least plan what tests you are going to make before you  code a function
57|- Don’t assume typing is correct until proven, or allow it to fail safe
58|- Failures should clear transparent and observable, every function doesnt need to intensly check it just needs to report failures accurately
59|- Tests must be consistent
60|- Integration test must reflect how a user could want to use the app
61|- Use the lowest possible level of tests( Ie Unit over api over e2e) for the fastest test cycle
62|
63|
64|## Fast iteration over long planning
65|
66|Sometimes you just can’t know what will happen without using it and that is essential. Spending too long planning can cause ideas to get confused or get you trapped in a loop where you just make plans worse.  Having simple clear checkpoints is great.
67|
68|### Principles
69|- When planning, factor in points to check certain things and how the plan can be adapted when needed
70|- Try and create safe ways to test functionality, ie not in prod, when possible as this will allow you to confirm things work.
71|- Focus on one small change at a time, get tests passing then work on the next element.
72|- Always design code with the intent it will be changed/replaced soon
73|- Minimise friction in development even if it is small
74|- Make change easy, then make the change. Even if making change easy is hard.
75|
76|
77|
78|# Inspirations
79|My principles here are inspired by:
80|
81|- Extreme programming Explained by Kent Beck (book)
82|- Life isn’t binary (book)
83|- Intent driven design by David whitney (Talk)
84|
85|
86|# Examples
87|
88|## Intent Driven descriptions
89|
90|### Bad Example
91|
92|```js
93|
94|const userInOneYearFactory = (name, age, users) => {
95|
96|    const user = {name: name , age: age + 1}
97|
98|    users.push(user)
99|  
100|}
101|
102|const list = []
103|
104|userFactory("Frank",32,list)
105|
106|
107|```
108|
109|## Good example
110|
111|```js
112|
113|/**
114|* MARK: calculateAgeNextYear
115|* @description calculates the age someone will be next year
116|* @example const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: 3})  
117|console.log(usersAgeNextYear) // 4
118|*/
119|const calculateAgeNextYear = ({ageNow}) => {
120|  const ageNextYear = ageNow + 1
121|  
122|  return ageNextYear
123|}
124|
125|const userObjectsList = []
126|
127|const usersName = "Frank"
128|const usersAge = 32
129|
130|const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: usersAge})
131|
132|userObjectsList.push({name: usersName, age: usersAge})
133|
134|
135|```

1|# Values
2|
3|## User understandable over technical language
4|
5|I feel like code should always be understandable by users as they are the ones who dictate process. So the goal of code should make it the most understandable with zero context as possible
6|
7|### Principles
8|
9|- Long variables names where needed to be descriptive
10|- Avoid using technical language such as “factory” or “barrel”
11|- Stick to a common language profile, (tasks always being tasks, stages always being stages etc)
12|- File structure should reflect the call stack
13|- Use of JSDocs to explain variables in pure english
14|- Include why things are done not just what is done
15|- Use a labelled data inport pattern (IE  `({varA , varB}) => {}`)
16|- NEVER MENTION DESIGN PATTERNS
17|- Use @example tags in js doc to easily explain functionality
18|- Every new export also carries a `MARK:` label in the same JSDoc block, sitting directly above the export (only whitespace between `*/` and `export`); `npm run check:jsdoc-example` (<1s) checks this before pushing — copy-paste shapes in docs/agent-docs/KB-Code-Standards.md §Documentation/Jsdoc
19|  
20|  
21|
22|## Functional over Object oreintated
23|
24|Although pure functional code can tend to insanity it is always important to note co-mingle state and functionality. Where possible state should leave in clearly defined places, and functions should show a clear line in how we move from one state to another. Traditional object oriented design mainly serves to gatekeep devs(or for game dev).
25|
26|### Principles
27|
28|- Try and avoid using classes where possible
29|- Currying can be used to create sudo classes, avoid that
30|- Functions should follow black box mentality, clear input delivers the same output with no side affects
31|- Treat variables as immutable unless they are clearly defined states.
32|- Functions should always be named with a verb in, as they are doing something
33|- Give the miniumn data to each function as possible. Pick off fields before invocation.
34|- Each function should only work to achieve its task, with a single responsibility
35|
36|
37|## Co-location over abstraction
38|
39|Although abstraction is an essential part of coding it should always only be done by business level intent, not just on functionality. Ideally if you pick a random file in the codebase you should only need to look at the one folder above it and one folder under it to get all the context on its functionality.
40|
41|### Principles
42|- Unit tests should always be placed next to the relevant file
43|- Generally functions called in a higher function should be placed in a folder of that functions name. IE if `funA.js` calls `funB.js` it should be `./funA/funB.js`
44|- Generic/helper functions should only be made if they are repeatedly doing the same thing.
45|- Helpers should be treated like react state and exist at the lowest level folder that is common in the hierarchy of the folders
46|- If abstracting it would take up more lines/characters than just embedding that line directly on a per file basis avoid doing it. IE don’t abstract a single line just because its repeated unless it has some complex logic like a regex.
47|- Don’t fear repetition of code
48|- Make sure the code is easily searchable for any given task. If I said modify the task history box in the ui it should  be easy and logical to figure out where that is.
49|- Use folders as a tool for organising
50|
51|## Tested over trusted 
52|
53|Functionality should not assumed to exist until it is tested and evidenced. “it should work” isn’t always reliable and we want to make sure there are no regressions. 
54|
55|### Principles
56|- Try and at least plan what tests you are going to make before you  code a function
57|- Don’t assume typing is correct until proven, or allow it to fail safe
58|- Failures should clear transparent and observable, every function doesnt need to intensly check it just needs to report failures accurately
59|- Tests must be consistent
60|- Integration test must reflect how a user could want to use the app
61|- Use the lowest possible level of tests( Ie Unit over api over e2e) for the fastest test cycle
62|
63|
64|## Fast iteration over long planning
65|
66|Sometimes you just can’t know what will happen without using it and that is essential. Spending too long planning can cause ideas to get confused or get you trapped in a loop where you just make plans worse.  Having simple clear checkpoints is great.
67|
68|### Principles
69|- When planning, factor in points to check certain things and how the plan can be adapted when needed
70|- Try and create safe ways to test functionality, ie not in prod, when possible as this will allow you to confirm things work.
71|- Focus on one small change at a time, get tests passing then work on the next element.
72|- Always design code with the intent it will be changed/replaced soon
73|- Minimise friction in development even if it is small
74|- Make change easy, then make the change. Even if making change easy is hard.
75|
76|
77|
78|# Inspirations
79|My principles here are inspired by:
80|
81|- Extreme programming Explained by Kent Beck (book)
82|- Life isn’t binary (book)
83|- Intent driven design by David whitney (Talk)
84|
85|
86|# Examples
87|
88|## Intent Driven descriptions
89|
90|### Bad Example
91|
92|```js
93|
94|const userInOneYearFactory = (name, age, users) => {
95|
96|    const user = {name: name , age: age + 1}
97|
98|    users.push(user)
99|  
100|}
101|
102|const list = []
103|
104|userFactory("Frank",32,list)
105|
106|
107|```
108|
109|## Good example
110|
111|```js
112|
113|/**
114|* MARK: calculateAgeNextYear
115|* @description calculates the age someone will be next year
116|* @example const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: 3})  
117|console.log(usersAgeNextYear) // 4
118|*/
119|const calculateAgeNextYear = ({ageNow}) => {
120|  const ageNextYear = ageNow + 1
121|  
122|  return ageNextYear
123|}
124|
125|const userObjectsList = []
126|
127|const usersName = "Frank"
128|const usersAge = 32
129|
130|const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: usersAge})
131|
132|userObjectsList.push({name: usersName, age: usersAge})
133|
134|
135|```

1|# Implementation Plan — In-assignment transient backend errors non-fatal to the runner (S4)
2|
3|Task: `78eac844-250a-44d1-810e-6f047eb5a59e`
4|Source problem: any in-try backend-call failure inside `executeAssignment` sends an interrupt and rethrows → process exit → systemd restart, so every LAN blip or backend restart window can kill a run (501 fetch failed + 16 Backend 502s since 11-19 on server2-alpha; proven 502 window 11-20 20:40:20–20:40:57 during backend build 637).
5|Survey input: [SURVEY.md](./SURVEY.md) (Round 1, q1–q4; `answers: {}` — unanswered, so the recommended options below are carried as assumptions pending confirmation).
6|
7|## Goal
8|
9|1. Transient backend errors (fetch-failed network errors, HTTP 502/503/504) raised during an assignment make `executeAssignment` send an interrupt WITH a reason and RETURN (keep polling) instead of rethrowing — the same report-and-return precedent as the `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` and deterministic-gitFailure branches.
10|2. The idle loop stops crash-cycling on backend outages: bounded retries with backoff for idempotent calls (dispatch poll; heartbeat already warn-continues), or at minimum sleep-and-continue instead of exit.
11|3. The non-fatal set is enumerated explicitly; `STALE_EPOCH`, auth failures, and genuinely unknown errors stay fatal. No inverted catch-all, so new failure modes stay loud.
12|4. Regression tests in `runner/client.backendOutage.test.js` (+ daemon fatality-boundary tests) prove the transient/fatal boundary, registered in `scripts/run-tests.mjs`.
13|
14|## Success Criteria
15|
16|- A 502/503/504 or dropped-socket failure from any backend call inside `executeAssignment` produces a best-effort `interrupt` carrying a reason, a one-line log naming the cause, and a return (no throw) — the dispatch loop keeps polling and the process stays alive.
17|- A dispatch-poll (`dispatchClaim`) transient failure backs off and re-polls without consuming idle budget and without exiting; restart counters stop incrementing across a backend restart window.
18|- `STALE_EPOCH` still propagates (epoch fencing intact), auth/credential failures still exit loud, and unknown errors still throw — proven by boundary tests asserting `rethrown === false` for transient and `rethrown === true` for stale-epoch.
19|- `node --test runner/client.backendOutage.test.js runner/daemon.test.js runner/client.test.js` passes, the repo unit gate (`npm test` via `scripts/run-tests.mjs`) passes, and the new suite file is registered (the `tests/run-tests.test.mjs` pin fails the gate if it is not).
20|- Post-rollout (needs PROD-READ-ONLY permission): crash-restart rate in the runner journal drops across backend restart windows while assignment success holds; E4 timestamp-join confirmed on `db24c124`, `1f8959ca`, `f56e9878`, `ef21e99b`, `bae668cb`.
21|
22|## Survey decisions (factored in)
23|
24|Local `SURVEY.md` Round 1 is unanswered (`"answers": {}`). This plan adopts the recommended option for each as a working assumption (flagged for confirmation in Open Questions). The stage brief also cites the source-task survey q5 ("survive network/502/503/504, keep the rest fatal") — that maps to local q2 and is adopted the same way.
25|
26|| # | Question | Adopted (recommended) answer | Plan effect |
27||---|----------|------------------------------|-------------|
28|| q1 | Mid-task connection drop: what should the worker do? | Stay alive, report what happened, keep checking for work | Interrupt-with-reason + return; never rethrow for the transient set. |
29|| q2 (= source q5) | Which problems to survive vs still stop for? | Only survive short connection problems (network errors, 502/503/504); still stop for login problems, outdated orders, anything unknown | Explicit non-fatal enumeration (`isTransientBackendError`); `STALE_EPOCH`/auth/unknown stay fatal. |
30|| q3 | Idle poll/heartbeat outage: what to do? | Retry a few times with growing waits, then keep waiting without restarting | Bounded retries with backoff on idempotent idle calls; minimum acceptable fallback is sleep-and-continue. |
31|| q4 (optional) | Log visibility for ride-through? | A clear one-line note naming the cause, then keep going | One `warn`/`error` line with cause + task/project IDs per ride-through; no per-retry spam (retry attempts at debug/quiet). |
32|
33|## Approach
34|
35|Follow "make the change easy, then make the change", and build on the db49d6c6 containment — do NOT land a second competing catch-restructure:
36|
37|1. **Easy first:** extract one shared `isTransientBackendError(err)` classifier (single home for the explicit non-fatal set) plus shared test fixtures (502-shape stub, dropped-socket stub), with zero behavior change. Land this refactor green before touching behavior.
38|2. **Then the change:** add one narrow branch in the `executeAssignment` catch using the classifier (interrupt-with-reason + return), mirroring the `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` block shape; same one-branch treatment for the `executeIntegrationAssignment` catch (parity, decided in Key Decision 4).
39|3. **Then the idle loop:** transient-aware handling in the `dispatchClaim` catch (backoff + re-poll, no idle-budget consumption); verify the heartbeat timer path already tolerates outages (it warns-and-continues today) and add bounded join-time retries only if the Step 0 probe shows join is a live crash path.
40|4. **Then proof:** `runner/client.backendOutage.test.js` + daemon boundary tests, registration in `scripts/run-tests.mjs`, red→green runs, full gates, rollout/confirm plan.
41|
42|No new dependencies, no new config flags (backoff constants are module-local), no schema/wire changes (the interrupt `reason` field already exists).
43|
44|## Evidence (what the research established)
45|
46|Verified in-repo this session (line numbers are the current checkout — re-verify at implementation time):
47|
48|- **In-assignment catch:** `executeAssignment` catch (`runner/daemon.js` ~2296–2453) special-cases `STALE_EPOCH` (rethrow, line 2298), `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` (interrupt-with-reason + return, lines 2299–2315), deterministic gitFailure (report + return, lines 2316–2376), `failedOutcome` (failed completion, lines 2377–2428), then the generic path: flush, best-effort interrupt with reason, **`throw err`** (lines 2441–2452). The S4 branch slots in just before the generic path, copying the `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` block shape.
49|- **db49d6c6 containment already landed (build on it):** `runDispatchLoop` wraps `executeAssignment` in try/catch (~3097–3153): `STALE_EPOCH` rethrows, anything else is logged and contained. So in dispatch mode a rethrow no longer exits — but the stage brief's crash path is still live in three places: (a) `dispatchClaim` unknown errors `throw err` at line 3018 → loop exits → systemd restart (this is the 366→367 crash-cycling); (b) `runSingleAssignment` has no loop, so any rethrow exits non-zero; (c) `joinAndHeartbeat` failures before the loop starts exit the process. S4 must target exactly these, not rework the db49 catch.
50|- **Client error shapes** (`runner/client.js` `call`, lines 17–40): non-2xx throws `Error` with `statusCode = res.status` and `code = data?.code ?? null` — so a 502 arrives as `{ statusCode: 502, code }`. A dropped socket / refused connection rejects `fetchImpl` itself (raw `TypeError: fetch failed`, `ECONNREFUSED`/`ECONNRESET` causes) with no `statusCode`. The classifier must cover both shapes.
51|- **Heartbeat already tolerates outages:** the periodic timer (`deliverSteers(...).catch(warn)`, lines 1241–1245) and claim renewal (`claimHeartbeat(...).then(warn)`, lines 796–808) both warn-and-continue; heartbeat failures ride the lease TTL. The idle-loop crash-cycling is the dispatch-poll path, not the heartbeat path.
52|- **Integration parity site:** `executeIntegrationAssignment` catch (~2655–2697) ends in the same interrupt + `throw err` (lines 2687–2696).
53|- **Fatality contract pinned by an existing test:** `runner/daemon.test.js` "never idles out with dispatchIdleLimit 0" throws a generic `persistent-loop-probe` error from `dispatchClaim` and asserts the loop rejects — unknown dispatch errors MUST keep throwing after S4 (consistent with q2). S4's dispatch branch must only catch the classifier-positive set.
54|- **Test seams to reuse:** `stubClient` / `fakeHarness` / `localRepo` / `loopConfig` helpers and the `waitFor` polling helper in `runner/daemon.test.js`; `stubFetch` + `ok`/`fail` helpers in `runner/client.test.js`.
55|- **Test registration:** `scripts/run-tests.mjs` "Unit Tests (runner)" (~lines 460–491) names every `runner/*.test.js` explicitly, and `tests/run-tests.test.mjs` pins that every suite file on disk is registered — a new `runner/client.backendOutage.test.js` must be added to that list or the gate fails.
56|- **Evidence gap (does not block):** the cited source-research folder `docs/tasks/2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4/` (`RESPONSE.md` S4, `WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md` Cause 4, `TDD-TEST-EXAMPLES.md`, `GUIDE-04-backend-unreachable-502.md`, `RESPONSE_SURVEY.md` q5) is absent from this checkout (verified: no such folder; repo-wide search for `backend-unreachable|WIDE_NET|Backend 502` finds nothing). The GUIDE-04 §2/§3 test shapes are therefore reconstructed from the stage brief plus the in-repo client shapes above; Step 0 re-derives the exact 502/dropped-socket fixtures from `runner/client.js` and Node fetch behavior rather than trusting the brief's prose. If the folder exists upstream, pull it in Step 0 and reconcile (shapes should match; any conflict is resolved in favor of the observed client behavior).
57|
58|## Key Decisions
59|
60|1. **Explicit non-fatal enumeration, never an inverted catch-all (survey q2).** One `isTransientBackendError(err)` predicate owns the set: `statusCode ∈ {502, 503, 504}` OR a network-layer failure (fetch rejection: `TypeError: fetch failed`, `ECONNREFUSED`/`ECONNRESET`/`ETIMEDOUT`/`EAI_AGAIN`/socket-hangup causes — exact list fixed in Step 0 from observed shapes). Everything else falls through to today's generic path. New failure modes stay loud by construction.
61|2. **Classifier lives next to the client, used by the daemon.** Recommended: export from `runner/client.js` (it defines the error shapes) and import in `runner/daemon.js`. Rejected: duplicating status checks at each catch site (drifts), or putting it in `shared/` (runner-only concern; no backend/wire change).
62|3. **In-assignment branch = interrupt-with-reason + return, copying `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED`.** Return shape `{ interrupted: true, executionId, epoch, reason, transient: true }` so the loop (and logs) can distinguish outage ride-through from other interrupts. The `transient` flag is additive and internal-only.
63|4. **`executeIntegrationAssignment` gets the same branch (parity).** Same classifier, same interrupt+return shape. Cost is a few lines; leaving it out would keep "backend restart kills an integrate job's process" as a known hole. (Single-shot mode still ends the process either way — see Decision 6.)
64|5. **Idle loop: bounded retries with backoff on idempotent calls (survey q3), minimum sleep-and-continue.** `dispatchClaim` classifier-positive errors: retry up to N (recommended 3) with growing waits (recommended 1s→2s→4s, capped at `pollMs`), then keep waiting (back off one `pollMs` and re-poll) without consuming idle budget and without exiting — mirroring the existing 429/`RUNNER_PAUSED` branches (lines 2980–2997). Join-time (`joinAndHeartbeat`) transient failures: add the same bounded retry at startup only if the Step 0 probe confirms join is a live crash path during outages; otherwise document as a follow-up, not scope creep.
65|6. **Fatal set unchanged: `STALE_EPOCH`, auth/credential failures, unknown errors.** `STALE_EPOCH` keeps propagating in all three catches (epoch fencing). Auth failures (401/credential rejection) exit loud — retrying them would spin forever on a revoked credential. Unknown errors keep the generic interrupt+rethrow path (and the `persistent-loop-probe` test keeps passing unmodified). `runSingleAssignment` keeps its non-zero-exit contract: a transient-interrupted result there maps to a clean non-zero exit with the reason (the process must end anyway with no loop to continue; the win is the task is released WITH a reason instead of crashing). Confirm this mapping in Open Questions if CI callers need `interrupted:true` to read as success.
66|7. **One-line log per ride-through (survey q4).** `logger.warn` (or `logger.error` where the sibling branches use it — match the `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` sink) naming cause + `projectId/taskId`; retry attempts stay quiet (or debug-level) so a 37s outage window does not spam the journal.

129|
130|Highest-risk validation: the Step 4 daemon boundary tests — `runDispatchLoop` is poll-driven, so bound the loop deterministically with the existing `stubClient`/`loopConfig({ dispatchPollMs: 1, dispatchIdleLimit })` seams (never wall-clock sleeps); follow the existing `runDispatchLoop` tests' count-then-succeed stub pattern.
131|
132|## Risks
133|
134|- **Over-matching the classifier (q2 trade-off):** an over-broad network set could swallow an auth or fencing failure and spin instead of exiting loud. Mitigation: allowlist only `502/503/504` + observed socket shapes; explicit negative tests for 401/`STALE_EPOCH`/429/500; match on stable `code`/`statusCode`, not message substrings.
135|- **Under-matching on undici version drift:** fetch-failure text varies by Node version. Mitigation: Step 0 derives shapes on the repo's pinned Node; predicate prefers `cause.code`/absence-of-`statusCode` signals.
136|- **Poison-task flap:** after S4, a persistently-502ing backend call re-queues the task each attempt (runner survives, task flaps until the backend heals). Strictly better than a restart storm; consecutive-failure backoff is out of scope (see Non-goals).
137|- **Interrupt-during-outage is best-effort by necessity:** the ride-through interrupt itself may 502; the lease TTL is the backstop (same as every sibling branch). The one-line log preserves discoverability.
138|- **Missing source research:** GUIDE-04 §2/§3 shapes are reconstructed (see Evidence gap). Mitigation: shapes are re-derived from the observed client code in Step 0; reconcile with upstream docs if they surface.
139|
140|## Non-goals
141|
142|- Any change to the db49d6c6 loop-level catch (it stays exactly as-is) or to `interrupt` → `complete(failed)` routing for generic errors.
143|- Retrying non-idempotent calls (`complete`, `interrupt` stay single-attempt best-effort); retries apply only to idempotent idle calls (dispatch poll, and join/heartbeat only per Step 3's probe).
144|- Consecutive-failure backoff/circuit-breaking for flapping tasks; treating HTTP 500 as transient.
145|- `--no-verify`, worktree, hook, or systemd unit changes.
146|- Running the PROD-READ-ONLY E4 timestamp-join or journal analysis without the permission grant.
147|
148|## Open Questions
149|
150|1. **Survey confirmation:** `SURVEY.md` answers are empty — confirm the four adopted recommended options (q1 stay-alive+report, q2 transient-only survival, q3 bounded backoff retries, q4 one-line log). If q3's simpler "just wait and re-check" is preferred, Step 3 collapses to the sleep-and-continue minimum with no retry counter. (Default if unanswered: proceed as planned.)
151|2. **Single-shot mapping (Decision 6):** confirm transient-interrupted in `runSingleAssignment` should exit non-zero with the reason (recommended, preserves the CI contract) rather than exit 0. If 0 is required, Step 2 skips the mapping.
152|3. **Retry budget (Decision 5):** confirm 3 attempts / 1s→2s→4s backoff for dispatch-poll retries, or name other bounds. Any reasonable bound fits the same code shape.
153|4. None other — all technical facts above were verified in-repo this session except the noted source-folder gap.
154|
155|## Work estimate / sequencing note
156|
157|Big/research pieces first per the stage brief: Step 0 (chain verification + exact error-shape derivation + upstream doc reconcile) and the Step 3 join-time probe are the riskiest and come before/around the small behavior edits. Steps 1–3 are small and mechanical once the classifier set is fixed. 5|# KainBain coding standards
6|
7|
8|## Architecture
9|The action should always be split by logical function not architectural feature. This means the architecture should have a natural call hierarchy, this is inspired by reacts component tree behaviours.
10|
11|This should be as functional as possible(within reason). Most things should largely look like state is external to the system, and ergo mostly stored in files. However due to readability concerns be careful to avoid 
12|
13|> **warning** Warning
14|> Keep an eye out for technical language (like factory, types or ...) this is a sign the architecture is not readable and should force a moment of pause to re-evaluate how you architect this change.
15|
16|
17|## Readability
18|Code should be readable with zero context and only minor technical knowledge. It should describe the business level logic of the code not the technical details for example:
19|```js
20|
21|const agentSessionIdentifier = getSessionIdentifier(SessionInstance)
22|
23|if (agentSessionIdentifier == "false"){
24|
25|  return {value: null , error: new Error("Session not found")}
26|}
27|
28|```
29|
30|To this end we should also make liberal use of JSDocs to describe variables and functions in plain English to assist. Extra important to use the `@example` and `@description` tags
31|
32|Example
33|```js
34|/***
35|* MARK: getSessionIdentifier
36|* @description Gets the unique id (UUIDv4) for a given instance
37|* @example console.log(getSessionIdentifier(SessionInstance)) => 892739292092
38|*
39|***/
40|
41|```
42|
43|Notice the use of MARK: since this is going to be viewed likely in vscode it is good to tailor the experience to that. `MARK:` for example creates a header in the minimap view of VScode
44|
45|
46|
47|
48|## Testing
49|First of all, all testing should not use a real live AI agent, and preferably use a mock. We will create a dedicated subset which are Ai agent included tests and those can only be run with explicit permission and thorough checks (as not to waste AI tokens)
50|
51|Largely the process of Test driven development should be followed, where you define the tests before you write the function. This because only by proving something with a test can you prove your function works and ergo the work is complete. An untested bit of code should be treated as broken 
52|
53|
54|### Unit Tests
55|This should be the majority of tests used as they are quick and easy. They are too be run regularly. 
56|
57|They should largely be black box tests, without influencing or testing how things work internally. This means we can judge log based tests as an anti pattern. 
58|
59|
60|### Canary E2E tests
61|
62|These are very simple e2e tests (excluding ai) that are just meant to mainly detect major errors and runtime errors. This is not a full end to end suite. These should mainly just assert no errors while touching as many things as possible, although ideally should be done in a way that doesn't need to be touched. 
63|
64|There needs to be a separate set of canary tests for every error boundary. At the start it'll just mainly render a ui/start the app and detect if there are things such as missing imports or other errors. After awhile you will need to do this on each boundary separately 
65|
66|### API tests
67|Although UI based tests take awhile to run, API tests can be quick and easy. They should just mock the the AI agent layer, the rest should be authentic e2e of the API. These are good for any new endpoints or changes in endpoint behaviour. These also serve as really good documentation.
68|
69|### screenshot generator 
70|Although these tests don't assert anything it is really useful to generate images so the app can be analysed. The tests should generate a screenshot per screen, for mobile, tablet and desktop views. 
71|
72|It should easily be extendable so we can do exploratory screenshots. This is the primary eyes on the app. 
73|
74|
75|## Documentation 
76|
77|### Jsdoc
78|As mentioned above Jsdoc should be used to make sure things are in line with business behaviour. Key to use examples and make them readable.
79|
80|**Enforced (WP-8 automated gates — not advisory):**
81|- `MARK:` + `@description` + `@example` on every public export (`export function/class/const/let/var/default`
82|  in `api/`, `shared/`, `frontend/src/`): enforced for all *new* exports by
83|  `npm run check:jsdoc-example` (wired into `npm run docs:check` and CI).
84|  Scope: any new exported item, including a new export added to an existing
85|  file — not just new files. The JSDoc block must sit directly above the
86|  export: only whitespace may sit between `*/` and `export`, or the gate does
87|  not see it. Every new block needs all three lines: a `MARK:` name (shows in
88|  the VSCode minimap), a `@description`, and a runnable `@example`.
89|  Pre-existing gaps are grandfathered in
90|  `scripts/baselines/jsdoc-example-missing.json` and shrink via `--prune`;
91|  never add a new export to that baseline (see §q6: new exports document
92|  themselves). Before pushing, run `npm run check:jsdoc-example` (<1s)
93|  whenever you add or rename an export — it is the same check CI runs, so a
94|  local PASS means CI will not fail on this gate. Reproduce/triage:
95|  `node scripts/check-jsdoc-example.mjs --report`.
96|
97|  Minimal compliant shapes (copy the block, paste it directly above the
98|  export, then fill in a real example — these are the same templates the gate
99|  failure message prints, pre-filled with your file and export name):
100|
101|  ```js
102|  /**
103|   * MARK: myExport
104|   * @description What myExport does.
105|   * @example myExport(input) => expectedOutput
106|   */
107|  export function myExport(input) { /* ... */ }
108|  ```
109|
110|  ```js
111|  /**
112|   * MARK: myValue
113|   * @description What myValue holds.
114|   * @example myValue => value
115|   */
116|  export const myValue = /* ... */;
117|  ```
118|
119|  Default exports use the file's base name (this is the exact shape that fixed
120|  the `TaskCompleteToggleButton` CI failure — the block goes above the
121|  `export default` line):
122|
123|  ```js
124|  /**
125|   * MARK: TaskCompleteToggleButton default
126|   * @description Default export of TaskCompleteToggleButton.
127|   * @example import TaskCompleteToggleButton from './TaskCompleteToggleButton';
128|   */
129|  export default TaskCompleteToggleButton;
130|  ```
131|- One function per file for newly added source files: at most one top-level
132|  named `function` declaration per new file in `api/`, `shared/`,
133|  `frontend/src/` (nested helpers and arrow constants are fine), enforced by
134|  `npm run check:one-function` (and CI). Pre-existing multi-function files are
135|  grandfathered in `scripts/allowlists/one-function-per-file.json` (q13);
136|  never add a new file to it — split the function into its own module instead.
137|
138|### open API/swagger
139|The API layer should have a fully documented API since this will allow for easier testing and the ability to abstract the API rather than needing to read the code every time. 
140|
141|### comments
142|Comments beyond Jsdoc should be kept to a minimum. It is preferred generally to have longer variables and a more descriptive architectural style. 
143|
144|### other 
145|Any other documents should be in the general document store under the projects section (projects/personal/kainbain)
146|
147|
148|#project/kainbain#codestandards #documentation #testing

9|The action should always be split by logical function not architectural feature. This means the architecture should have a natural call hierarchy, this is inspired by reacts component tree behaviours.
10|
11|This should be as functional as possible(within reason). Most things should largely look like state is external to the system, and ergo mostly stored in files. However due to readability concerns be careful to avoid 
12|
13|> **warning** Warning
14|> Keep an eye out for technical language (like factory, types or ...) this is a sign the architecture is not readable and should force a moment of pause to re-evaluate how you architect this change.
15|
16|
17|## Readability
18|Code should be readable with zero context and only minor technical knowledge. It should describe the business level logic of the code not the technical details for example:
19|```js
20|
21|const agentSessionIdentifier = getSessionIdentifier(SessionInstance)
22|
23|if (agentSessionIdentifier == "false"){
24|
25|  return {value: null , error: new Error("Session not found")}
26|}
27|
28|```
29|
30|To this end we should also make liberal use of JSDocs to describe variables and functions in plain English to assist. Extra important to use the `@example` and `@description` tags
31|
32|Example
33|```js
34|/***
35|* MARK: getSessionIdentifier
36|* @description Gets the unique id (UUIDv4) for a given instance
37|* @example console.log(getSessionIdentifier(SessionInstance)) => 892739292092
38|*
39|***/
40|
41|```
42|
43|Notice the use of MARK: since this is going to be viewed likely in vscode it is good to tailor the experience to that. `MARK:` for example creates a header in the minimap view of VScode
44|
45|
46|
47|
48|## Testing
49|First of all, all testing should not use a real live AI agent, and preferably use a mock. We will create a dedicated subset which are Ai agent included tests and those can only be run with explicit permission and thorough checks (as not to waste AI tokens)
50|
51|Largely the process of Test driven development should be followed, where you define the tests before you write the function. This because only by proving something with a test can you prove your function works and ergo the work is complete. An untested bit of code should be treated as broken 
52|
53|
54|### Unit Tests
55|This should be the majority of tests used as they are quick and easy. They are too be run regularly. 
56|
57|They should largely be black box tests, without influencing or testing how things work internally. This means we can judge log based tests as an anti pattern. 
58|
59|
60|### Canary E2E tests
61|
62|These are very simple e2e tests (excluding ai) that are just meant to mainly detect major errors and runtime errors. This is not a full end to end suite. These should mainly just assert no errors while touching as many things as possible, although ideally should be done in a way that doesn't need to be touched. 
63|
64|There needs to be a separate set of canary tests for every error boundary. At the start it'll just mainly render a ui/start the app and detect if there are things such as missing imports or other errors. After awhile you will need to do this on each boundary separately 
65|
66|### API tests
67|Although UI based tests take awhile to run, API tests can be quick and easy. They should just mock the the AI agent layer, the rest should be authentic e2e of the API. These are good for any new endpoints or changes in endpoint behaviour. These also serve as really good documentation.
68|
69|### screenshot generator 
70|Although these tests don't assert anything it is really useful to generate images so the app can be analysed. The tests should generate a screenshot per screen, for mobile, tablet and desktop views. 
71|
72|It should easily be extendable so we can do exploratory screenshots. This is the primary eyes on the app. 
73|
74|
75|## Documentation 
76|
77|### Jsdoc
78|As mentioned above Jsdoc should be used to make sure things are in line with business behaviour. Key to use examples and make them readable.
79|
80|**Enforced (WP-8 automated gates — not advisory):**
81|- `MARK:` + `@description` + `@example` on every public export (`export function/class/const/let/var/default`
82|  in `api/`, `shared/`, `frontend/src/`): enforced for all *new* exports by
83|  `npm run check:jsdoc-example` (wired into `npm run docs:check` and CI).
84|  Scope: any new exported item, including a new export added to an existing
85|  file — not just new files. The JSDoc block must sit directly above the
86|  export: only whitespace may sit between `*/` and `export`, or the gate does
87|  not see it. Every new block needs all three lines: a `MARK:` name (shows in
88|  the VSCode minimap), a `@description`, and a runnable `@example`.
89|  Pre-existing gaps are grandfathered in
90|  `scripts/baselines/jsdoc-example-missing.json` and shrink via `--prune`;
91|  never add a new export to that baseline (see §q6: new exports document
92|  themselves). Before pushing, run `npm run check:jsdoc-example` (<1s)
93|  whenever you add or rename an export — it is the same check CI runs, so a
94|  local PASS means CI will not fail on this gate. Reproduce/triage:
95|  `node scripts/check-jsdoc-example.mjs --report`.
96|
97|  Minimal compliant shapes (copy the block, paste it directly above the
98|  export, then fill in a real example — these are the same templates the gate
99|  failure message prints, pre-filled with your file and export name):
100|
101|  ```js
102|  /**
103|   * MARK: myExport
104|   * @description What myExport does.
105|   * @example myExport(input) => expectedOutput
106|   */
107|  export function myExport(input) { /* ... */ }
108|  ```
109|
110|  ```js
111|  /**
112|   * MARK: myValue
113|   * @description What myValue holds.
114|   * @example myValue => value
115|   */
116|  export const myValue = /* ... */;
117|  ```
118|
119|  Default exports use the file's base name (this is the exact shape that fixed
120|  the `TaskCompleteToggleButton` CI failure — the block goes above the
121|  `export default` line):
122|
123|  ```js
124|  /**
125|   * MARK: TaskCompleteToggleButton default
126|   * @description Default export of TaskCompleteToggleButton.
127|   * @example import TaskCompleteToggleButton from './TaskCompleteToggleButton';
128|   */
129|  export default TaskCompleteToggleButton;
130|  ```
131|- One function per file for newly added source files: at most one top-level
132|  named `function` declaration per new file in `api/`, `shared/`,
133|  `frontend/src/` (nested helpers and arrow constants are fine), enforced by
134|  `npm run check:one-function` (and CI). Pre-existing multi-function files are
135|  grandfathered in `scripts/allowlists/one-function-per-file.json` (q13);
136|  never add a new file to it — split the function into its own module instead.
137|
138|### open API/swagger
139|The API layer should have a fully documented API since this will allow for easier testing and the ability to abstract the API rather than needing to read the code every time. 
140|
141|### comments
142|Comments beyond Jsdoc should be kept to a minimum. It is preferred generally to have longer variables and a more descriptive architectural style. 
143|
144|### other 
145|Any other documents should be in the general document store under the projects section (projects/personal/kainbain)
146|
147|
148|#project/kainbain#codestandards #documentation #testing

# KainBain coding standards


## Architecture
The action should always be split by logical function not architectural feature. This means the architecture should have a natural call hierarchy, this is inspired by reacts component tree behaviours.

This should be as functional as possible(within reason). Most things should largely look like state is external to the system, and ergo mostly stored in files. However due to readability concerns be careful to avoid 

> **warning** Warning
> Keep an eye out for technical language (like factory, types or ...) this is a sign the architecture is not readable and should force a moment of pause to re-evaluate how you architect this change.


## Readability
Code should be readable with zero context and only minor technical knowledge. It should describe the business level logic of the code not the technical details for example:
```js

const agentSessionIdentifier = getSessionIdentifier(SessionInstance)

if (agentSessionIdentifier == "false"){

  return {value: null , error: new Error("Session not found")}
}

```

To this end we should also make liberal use of JSDocs to describe variables and functions in plain English to assist. Extra important to use the `@example` and `@description` tags

Example
```js
/***
* MARK: getSessionIdentifier
* @description Gets the unique id (UUIDv4) for a given instance
* @example console.log(getSessionIdentifier(SessionInstance)) => 892739292092
*
***/

```

Notice the use of MARK: since this is going to be viewed likely in vscode it is good to tailor the experience to that. `MARK:` for example creates a header in the minimap view of VScode




## Testing
First of all, all testing should not use a real live AI agent, and preferably use a mock. We will create a dedicated subset which are Ai agent included tests and those can only be run with explicit permission and thorough checks (as not to waste AI tokens)

Largely the process of Test driven development should be followed, where you define the tests before you write the function. This because only by proving something with a test can you prove your function works and ergo the work is complete. An untested bit of code should be treated as broken 


### Unit Tests
This should be the majority of tests used as they are quick and easy. They are too be run regularly. 

They should largely be black box tests, without influencing or testing how things work internally. This means we can judge log based tests as an anti pattern. 


### Canary E2E tests

These are very simple e2e tests (excluding ai) that are just meant to mainly detect major errors and runtime errors. This is not a full end to end suite. These should mainly just assert no errors while touching as many things as possible, although ideally should be done in a way that doesn't need to be touched. 

There needs to be a separate set of canary tests for every error boundary. At the start it'll just mainly render a ui/start the app and detect if there are things such as missing imports or other errors. After awhile you will need to do this on each boundary separately 

### API tests
Although UI based tests take awhile to run, API tests can be quick and easy. They should just mock the the AI agent layer, the rest should be authentic e2e of the API. These are good for any new endpoints or changes in endpoint behaviour. These also serve as really good documentation.

### screenshot generator 
Although these tests don't assert anything it is really useful to generate images so the app can be analysed. The tests should generate a screenshot per screen, for mobile, tablet and desktop views. 

It should easily be extendable so we can do exploratory screenshots. This is the primary eyes on the app. 


## Documentation 

### Jsdoc
As mentioned above Jsdoc should be used to make sure things are in line with business behaviour. Key to use examples and make them readable.

**Enforced (WP-8 automated gates — not advisory):**
- `MARK:` + `@description` + `@example` on every public export (`export function/class/const/let/var/default`
  in `api/`, `shared/`, `frontend/src/`): enforced for all *new* exports by
  `npm run check:jsdoc-example` (wired into `npm run docs:check` and CI).
  Scope: any new exported item, including a new export added to an existing
  file — not just new files. The JSDoc block must sit directly above the
  export: only whitespace may sit between `*/` and `export`, or the gate does
  not see it. Every new block needs all three lines: a `MARK:` name (shows in
  the VSCode minimap), a `@description`, and a runnable `@example`.
  Pre-existing gaps are grandfathered in
  `scripts/baselines/jsdoc-example-missing.json` and shrink via `--prune`;
  never add a new export to that baseline (see §q6: new exports document
  themselves). Before pushing, run `npm run check:jsdoc-example` (<1s)
  whenever you add or rename an export — it is the same check CI runs, so a
  local PASS means CI will not fail on this gate. Reproduce/triage:
  `node scripts/check-jsdoc-example.mjs --report`.

  Minimal compliant shapes (copy the block, paste it directly above the
  export, then fill in a real example — these are the same templates the gate
  failure message prints, pre-filled with your file and export name):

  ```js
  /**
   * MARK: myExport
   * @description What myExport does.
   * @example myExport(input) => expectedOutput
   */
  export function myExport(input) { /* ... */ }
  ```

# KainBain coding standards


## Architecture
The action should always be split by logical function not architectural feature. This means the architecture should have a natural call hierarchy, this is inspired by reacts component tree behaviours.

This should be as functional as possible(within reason). Most things should largely look like state is external to the system, and ergo mostly stored in files. However due to readability concerns be careful to avoid 

> **warning** Warning
> Keep an eye out for technical language (like factory, types or ...) this is a sign the architecture is not readable and should force a moment of pause to re-evaluate how you architect this change.


## Readability
Code should be readable with zero context and only minor technical knowledge. It should describe the business level logic of the code not the technical details for example:
```js

const agentSessionIdentifier = getSessionIdentifier(SessionInstance)

if (agentSessionIdentifier == "false"){

  return {value: null , error: new Error("Session not found")}
}

```

To this end we should also make liberal use of JSDocs to describe variables and functions in plain English to assist. Extra important to use the `@example` and `@description` tags

Example
```js
/***
* MARK: getSessionIdentifier
* @description Gets the unique id (UUIDv4) for a given instance
* @example console.log(getSessionIdentifier(SessionInstance)) => 892739292092
*
***/

```

Notice the use of MARK: since this is going to be viewed likely in vscode it is good to tailor the experience to that. `MARK:` for example creates a header in the minimap view of VScode




## Testing
First of all, all testing should not use a real live AI agent, and preferably use a mock. We will create a dedicated subset which are Ai agent included tests and those can only be run with explicit permission and thorough checks (as not to waste AI tokens)

Largely the process of Test driven development should be followed, where you define the tests before you write the function. This because only by proving something with a test can you prove your function works and ergo the work is complete. An untested bit of code should be treated as broken 


### Unit Tests
This should be the majority of tests used as they are quick and easy. They are too be run regularly. 

They should largely be black box tests, without influencing or testing how things work internally. This means we can judge log based tests as an anti pattern. 


### Canary E2E tests

These are very simple e2e tests (excluding ai) that are just meant to mainly detect major errors and runtime errors. This is not a full end to end suite. These should mainly just assert no errors while touching as many things as possible, although ideally should be done in a way that doesn't need to be touched. 

There needs to be a separate set of canary tests for every error boundary. At the start it'll just mainly render a ui/start the app and detect if there are things such as missing imports or other errors. After awhile you will need to do this on each boundary separately 

### API tests
Although UI based tests take awhile to run, API tests can be quick and easy. They should just mock the the AI agent layer, the rest should be authentic e2e of the API. These are good for any new endpoints or changes in endpoint behaviour. These also serve as really good documentation.

### screenshot generator 
Although these tests don't assert anything it is really useful to generate images so the app can be analysed. The tests should generate a screenshot per screen, for mobile, tablet and desktop views. 

It should easily be extendable so we can do exploratory screenshots. This is the primary eyes on the app. 


## Documentation 

### Jsdoc
As mentioned above Jsdoc should be used to make sure things are in line with business behaviour. Key to use examples and make them readable.

**Enforced (WP-8 automated gates — not advisory):**
- `MARK:` + `@description` + `@example` on every public export (`export function/class/const/let/var/default`
  in `api/`, `shared/`, `frontend/src/`): enforced for all *new* exports by
  `npm run check:jsdoc-example` (wired into `npm run docs:check` and CI).
  Scope: any new exported item, including a new export added to an existing
  file — not just new files. The JSDoc block must sit directly above the
  export: only whitespace may sit between `*/` and `export`, or the gate does
  not see it. Every new block needs all three lines: a `MARK:` name (shows in
  the VSCode minimap), a `@description`, and a runnable `@example`.
  Pre-existing gaps are grandfathered in
  `scripts/baselines/jsdoc-example-missing.json` and shrink via `--prune`;
  never add a new export to that baseline (see §q6: new exports document
  themselves). Before pushing, run `npm run check:jsdoc-example` (<1s)
  whenever you add or rename an export — it is the same check CI runs, so a
  local PASS means CI will not fail on this gate. Reproduce/triage:
  `node scripts/check-jsdoc-example.mjs --report`.

  Minimal compliant shapes (copy the block, paste it directly above the
  export, then fill in a real example — these are the same templates the gate
  failure message prints, pre-filled with your file and export name):

  ```js
  /**
   * MARK: myExport
   * @description What myExport does.
   * @example myExport(input) => expectedOutput
   */
  export function myExport(input) { /* ... */ }
  ```

34|
35|- `packageRunner` copies `runner/`, `shared/`, `api/` with pruning of `*.test.js`/`*.spec.js` (see `copyPruned`/`assertClean`), so the new `runner/client.backendOutage.test.js` never ships. `INSTALL.txt` and the leg-closure (`RUNNER_LEG_BUNDLED_DEPS`) are untouched; no new bare imports were added (`daemon.js` -> `./client.js` is a relative import present in every bundle).

40|
41|- `runner/client.js` `call` still sends identical paths/bodies/headers and still throws `{statusCode, code}` on non-2xx. The new predicate only reads `statusCode`/`code`/`cause.code`; it changes no request bytes.

54|| Bundle layout | No new runtime files; edited files ship together in one tarball so `daemon.js` -> `./client.js` always resolves. | No |

56|| Idle: dispatch-poll retry | `[1000,2000,4000]` capped to `pollMs`, then `polls+=1` + `sleep(pollMs)` + `continue` without consuming idle budget (same shape as the existing `429`/`RUNNER_PAUSED` branches). Unknown errors still hit `throw err` (`persistent-loop-probe` test unmodified). Process stays alive through a long outage instead of systemd-restarting — intended behavior, polls resume on heal. | No (intended liveness change, not a brick) |
57|| In-assignment: `executeAssignment`/`executeIntegrationAssignment` | Transient -> best-effort `interrupt` with reason + `return {interrupted:true,...,transient:true}` instead of rethrow. The interrupt itself is swallowed if it also 502s (lease TTL is the backstop, same as sibling branches). Task is released via the identical re-queue path as before. | No |
58|| Single-shot: `runSingleAssignment` | Transient-interrupted maps to `throw new Error(reason)` (non-zero exit preserved), matching the pre-existing non-zero contract where the raw backend error used to propagate. Error *text* changes from e.g. `Backend 502 on ...` to `Backend unreachable mid-assignment: ...`; CI callers branching on the old exact string would see a different message but still a failure exit. Not an install break. | No |
59|| Logging | One warn/error line per ride-through naming cause + ids; retries stay quiet. No log-volume contract break. | No |
60|| Rollback | `previous` still points at the `0.2.0` tree; state is symmetric; manual/rollback flip restores byte-identical old code. | No |
61|| Tests / gates (`run-tests.mjs`, `publish.sh`) | Both lists now name `runner/client.backendOutage.test.js`; nothing here runs inside already-installed trees. (Prior CI failure in `tests/publish.test.mjs` was a list-pin mismatch at that time; the branch's `publish.sh` update aligns the lists — a gate-strictness item for the next CI run, not an install-safety issue.) | No |
62|
63|## Deliberate-shape checks (why these cannot brick installs)
64|
65|- **Classifier is allowlist-only.** `statusCode` present -> transient iff in `{502,503,504}`; otherwise the cause chain (depth 4) must carry a known `ECONN*`/`UND_ERR_*` code. `STALE_EPOCH`/409, 401/403 auth, 429, 500, and unknown errors all return `false` by construction, so new failure modes stay loud instead of spinning. A bare `TypeError: fetch failed` with no recognized code (e.g. misconfigured `backendUrl`) also returns `false` — ambiguous failures keep exiting loud.
66|- **No persistence drift.** The outage cause helper (`describeBackendOutageCause`) is pure string building with `redactSecretsText`; nothing new is written to disk.
67|- **Bounded by construction.** Both retry loops are capped arrays; the idle path always sleeps `pollMs` and re-polls, so a dead backend cannot create a hot loop (same backoff shape as the pre-existing `429` branch).
68|- **db49d6c6 not reworked.** The loop-level catch around `executeAssignment` is untouched by this diff; S4 only adds branches inside the assignment catches and the dispatch-poll catch, per the plan constraint.
69|

71|

73|- `runner/updates/{index,manifest,state}.js`, `runner/main.js`, `runner/credentialFile.js`, `runner/config.js`, `scripts/package-runner.mjs`, `runner/bin/kainbain-runner`, `api/flow/runnerVersionCompat.js`, `api/version.json`, `.env.example` version knobs — all confirming no gating, schema, or contract change.
74|- `runner/daemon.test.js` added tests assert single-shot still exits non-zero on transient, unknown dispatch errors still throw, and `STALE_EPOCH` still propagates (boundary pinned). No existing test assertions were rewritten to hide a contract change (diff is additive in `daemon.test.js`).
75|

77|
78|## Conclusion
79|
80|The current `0.2.1` implementation is a backward-compatible, runner-only patch: same backend range, same config/credential/state contracts, same bundle shape, bounded retries, unchanged audit of fatal paths, and clean rollback. Existing installs can update in place via the self-update channel, fresh installs extract the same layout, and a failed `0.2.1` boot still rolls back to `0.2.0`. Nothing in the diff requires a paired backend upgrade, env-file rewrite, credential re-collection, or manual intervention.

4|Source problem: any in-try backend-call failure inside `executeAssignment` sends an interrupt and rethrows → process exit → systemd restart, so every LAN blip or backend restart window can kill a run (501 fetch failed + 16 Backend 502s since 11-19 on server2-alpha; proven 502 window 11-20 20:40:20–20:40:57 during backend build 637).

7|## Goal
8|
9|1. 10|2. The idle loop stops crash-cycling on backend outages: bounded retries with backoff for idempotent calls (dispatch poll; heartbeat already warn-continues), or at minimum sleep-and-continue instead of exit.
11|3. The non-fatal set is enumerated explicitly; `STALE_EPOCH`, auth failures, and genuinely unknown errors stay fatal. No inverted catch-all, so new failure modes stay loud.

13|
14|## Success Criteria
15|
16|- A 502/503/504 or dropped-socket failure from any backend call inside `executeAssignment` produces a best-effort `interrupt` carrying a reason, a one-line log naming the cause, and a return (no throw) — the dispatch loop keeps polling and the process stays alive.
17|- A dispatch-poll (`dispatchClaim`) transient failure backs off and re-polls without consuming idle budget and without exiting; restart counters stop incrementing across a backend restart window.
18|- `STALE_EPOCH` still propagates (epoch fencing intact), auth/credential failures still exit loud, and unknown errors still throw — proven by boundary tests asserting `rethrown === false` for transient and `rethrown === true` for stale-epoch.

22|## Survey decisions (factored in)

24|Local `SURVEY.md` Round 1 is unanswered (`"answers": {}`). This plan adopts the recommended option for each as a working assumption (flagged for confirmation in Open Questions). 130|Highest-risk validation: the Step 4 daemon boundary tests — `runDispatchLoop` is poll-driven, so bound the loop deterministically with the existing `stubClient`/`loopConfig({ dispatchPollMs: 1, dispatchIdleLimit })` seams (never wall-clock sleeps); follow the existing `runDispatchLoop` tests' count-then-succeed stub pattern.
131|
132|## Risks
133|
134|- **Over-matching the classifier (q2 trade-off):** an over-broad network set could swallow an auth or fencing failure and spin instead of exiting loud. 137|- **Interrupt-during-outage is best-effort by necessity:** the ride-through interrupt itself may 502; the lease TTL is the backstop (same as every sibling branch). The one-line log preserves discoverability.
138|- **Missing source research:** GUIDE-04 §2/§3 shapes are reconstructed (see Evidence gap). Mitigation: shapes are re-derived from the observed client code in Step 0; reconcile with upstream docs if they surface.
139|
140|## Non-goals
141|
142|- Any change to the db49d6c6 loop-level catch (it stays exactly as-is) or to `interrupt` → `complete(failed)` routing for generic errors.
143|- Retrying non-idempotent calls (`complete`, `interrupt` stay single-attempt best-effort); retries apply only to idempotent idle calls (dispatch poll, and join/heartbeat only per Step 3's probe).

145|- `--no-verify`, worktree, hook, or systemd unit changes.
146|- Running the PROD-READ-ONLY E4 timestamp-join or journal analysis without the permission grant.

148|## Open Questions
149|
150|1. **Survey confirmation:** `SURVEY.md` answers are empty — confirm the four adopted recommended options (q1 stay-alive+report, q2 transient-only survival, q3 bounded backoff retries, q4 one-line log). If q3's simpler "just wait and re-check" is preferred, Step 3 collapses to the sleep-and-continue minimum with no retry counter. (Default if unanswered: proceed as planned.)

152|3. **Retry budget (Decision 5):** confirm 3 attempts / 1s→2s→4s backoff for dispatch-poll retries, or name other bounds. Any reasonable bound fits the same code shape.

154|

156|
157|Big/research pieces first per the stage brief: Step 0 (chain verification + exact error-shape derivation + upstream doc reconcile) and the Step 3 join-time probe are the riskiest and come before/around the small behavior edits. +	"ENETUNREACH",

+	"UND_ERR_SOCKET",

+	"UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT",
+	"UND_ERR_BODY_TIMEOUT",
+]);

+ * MARK: isTransientBackendError

+ *   network-layer fetch rejections where the backend never answered

+ *   INVALID_CREDENTIAL, 403), 429, 500, and unknown errors stay fatal
+ *   by construction, so new failure modes stay loud. Pure predicate:

+	// transient — 401/403/409/429/500 and friends stay fatal/loud.

+const TRANSIENT_BACKEND_STATUSES = new Set([502, 503, 504]);
+// Node system codes (ECONN*) plus undici fetch-failure codes (UND_ERR_*,
+// e.g. a destroyed socket surfaces as UND_ERR_SOCKET on Node 20/22/24).
+// Deliberately NOT matched: bare `TypeError: fetch failed` with no
+// recognized code (e.g. a misconfigured backendUrl) — ambiguous failures
+// stay loud rather than spinning the loop forever.
+const TRANSIENT_NETWORK_CODES = new Set([
+	"ECONNREFUSED",
+	"ECONNRESET",
+	"ETIMEDOUT",
+	"EAI_AGAIN",
+	"ENOTFOUND",
+	"EPIPE",
+	"EHOSTUNREACH",
+	"ENETUNREACH",
+	"ENETDOWN",
+	"UND_ERR_SOCKET",
+	"UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT",
+	"UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT",
+	"UND_ERR_BODY_TIMEOUT",
+]);
+
+/***
+ * MARK: isTransientBackendError
+ * @description Explicit non-fatal set for backend outages (S4): HTTP
+ *   502/503/504 (the backend or its proxy is restarting) plus
+ *   network-layer fetch rejections where the backend never answered
+ *   (refused/reset connection, timeout, DNS failure, dropped socket —
+ *   matched on stable `code`/`cause.code` signals, never message text).
+ *   Everything else returns false — STALE_EPOCH, auth rejections (401
+ *   INVALID_CREDENTIAL, 403), 429, 500, and unknown errors stay fatal
+ *   by construction, so new failure modes stay loud. Pure predicate:
+ *   no logging, no dependencies.
+ * @example isTransientBackendError(Object.assign(new Error('x'), { statusCode: 502 })) => true
+ * @param {*} err - Thrown value from a backend call.
+ * @returns {boolean} True only for the enumerated transient set.
+ ***/
+export function isTransientBackendError(err) {
+	if (!err || (typeof err !== "object" && typeof err !== "function")) return false;
+	// A status means the backend answered: only gateway outages are
+	// transient — 401/403/409/429/500 and friends stay fatal/loud.
+	const status = Number(err.statusCode);
+	if (Number.isFinite(status)) return TRANSIENT_BACKEND_STATUSES.has(status);
+	// No status: fetchImpl itself rejected. Walk the cause chain (undici
+	// nests the system error under `cause`) for a recognized code.
+	let current = err;
+	for (let depth = 0; depth < 4 && current && (typeof current === "object" || typeof current === "function"); depth += 1) {
+		if (typeof current.code === "string" && TRANSIENT_NETWORK_CODES.has(current.code)) return true;
+		current = current.cause;
+	}
+	return false;
+}
